articles.title: Brewers Among 5 2026 MLB Postseason Teams With Longest World Series Droughts
articles.summary: Nearly half of the 2026 MLB playoff field has gone at least 20 years without a World Series championship, but only one can reset that counter this October.
articles.body: At the end of the 2026 MLB playoffs, odds are good that a team that hasn’t won a championship for a long time could hoist the Commissioner’s Trophy. Of the 18 MLB teams to go at least 20 years without a World Series championship, five are participating in this year's postseason. Let’s look at those 18 teams; for most, 2026 is already another season without a title, but for the others there's still hope that October will deliver a championship. Cleveland Guardians, 77 seasons (1948) The last time that the Guardians were World Series champions was 1948. The last-living player from that team, Eddie Robinson, passed away in 2021. The 1948 season was so long ago that the team they defeated, the Braves, were still playing in Boston. Cleveland has certainly had chances since 1948 to become champs once more — they lost the 1954 World Series to the New York Giants, the ‘95 Fall Classic to the Braves, ‘97’s to the Marlins and 2016’s to the Cubs, snapping Chicago’s own 107-year title drought. Cleveland also lost in the ALCS in 1998, 2007 and 2024. There have been some great teams in Cleveland in the last 30-plus years, but to this point, none of them have come away with a championship. The 2026 iteration of the Guardians will get another chance to end the drought, though: Cleveland won its third AL Central title in three years, powered by (when healthy) third baseman José Ramírez , rookie and All-Star second baseman Travis Bazzana, outfielders Steven Kwan and Chase DeLauter and a rotation led by Parker Messick. Milwaukee Brewers, 57 seasons The Brewers have never won a World Series. Introduced in 1969 as the Seattle Pilots, the team moved to Milwaukee and was renamed in 1970. They first made the postseason in 1981, then lost in the World Series in ‘82. While they have made it to the playoffs nine times between 2008 and 2025, they made it to the NLCS just three times, and never beyond it — Milwaukee’s pennant drought isn’t quite as lengthy as their championship one, but it spans parts of five decades, too. The Brewers finished the 2026 regular season with the best record in baseball and Milwaukee's first-ever 100-win campaign, earning a first-round bye in this year’s postseason. They will take on the winner of the Padres-Cubs NL Wild Card Series as they seek to end the longest title drought for any team that has never won a championship in their history… one they share with another franchise. San Diego Padres, 57 seasons The Padres were also brought into MLB in 1969, and they, like the Brewers, have yet to win a World Series. San Diego has made it to the Fall Classic on two occasions, both of which were unfortunate for them: in 1984, they took on the 104-win, juggernaut Tigers, and in 1998 it was one of the greatest teams ever in the 114-win Yankees. Unsurprisingly, the Padres have a 1-8 record in World Series games. They will take on the Cubs in the NL Wild Card Series in 2026, just as in 2025, with the winner going on to face the Brewers in the NL Division Series once again. It’s entirely possible that the two 1969 expansion clubs face off there, with one team bumping their years without a title figure to 58, and the other either delaying the inevitable or finally raising its first championship banner. Seattle Mariners, 50 seasons The Mariners are another expansion team — introduced in 1977 — that has never won a World Series. Unlike the Padres or Brewers, however, Seattle has never even made it to the Fall Classic: they made it to three AL Championship Series between 1995 and 2001, and lost all three, then repeated that feat in 2025 by falling to the Blue Jays. The 2025 season marked just the second time that the team had even made it to the playoffs since 2001’s disappointment, and the 2026 season saw Seattle finish 10 games under .500 and in third in the AL West. Pittsburgh Pirates, 47 seasons (1979) The Pirates didn’t qualify for the postseason in 2026, so they are already at 47 seasons without a championship. That 1979 championship club had Hall of Famers Willie Stargell and Dave Parker in the lineup, with another, Bert Blyleven, leading the rotation — and Blyleven was just third in that Bucs’ rotation in ERA, despite his ‘79 being a fine season. Pittsburgh lost three consecutive NLCS from 1991 through 1993, then failed to make it past the NLDS in three straight years from 2013 through 2015. They haven’t made it to the postseason, otherwise, since their title in 1979, but at least finished over .500 in 2026 at 82-80. Baltimore Orioles, 43 seasons (1983) The Orioles improved on 2025's last-place finish by ending 2026 in fourth in the AL East, but Baltimore's championship drought was extended another year. The last time that Baltimore won a World Series, Cal Ripken Jr. was just 22 years old, in his second full year in the majors and all of 280 games into what would become a record 2,632 consecutive games played in the majors. Cal Ripken Jr. retired after the 2001 season. Detroit Tigers, 42 seasons (1984) The Tigers are a fascinating case, as they have been to the World Series 11 times and won it on four occasions, but you have to remember that the franchise has also existed since 1901, predating the World Series itself. They last won in 1984, against Tony Gwynn’s Padres, then lost the 2006 Fall Classic to the Cardinals and 2012’s to the Giants. Detroit was expected to contend in 2026 after making it to the postseason for the second year in a row in 2025, but despite an excellent rookie campaign from infielder Kevin McGonigle, the Tigers struggled for too long this season to sustain a serious run, and sold off starters Tarik Skubal and Casey Mize at the deadline. New York Mets, 40 seasons (1986) The Mets suffered injuries and struggled for much of 2026, dashing postseason hopes early on — the last time that New York won the World Series was in 1986 against the Red Sox. They have had opportunities since, as they lost the World Series in 2000 against the Yankees and in 2015 against the Royals. Athletics, 37 seasons (1989) Here are two facts that are difficult to reconcile if you’re under 45 years old or so: Despite the lengthy drought, the A’s have more titles than the Dodgers and more than the Giants, with only the Yankees and Cardinals ahead of them. Cincinnati Reds, 36 seasons (1990) The last time the Reds won a World Series, they did so against the Athletics — Cincinnati is the reason that the A’s drought isn’t one year shorter than it is! The Reds will have to wait at least one more year, too, as the team finished in last place in the NL Central in 2026, despite the best season of star shortstop Elly De La Cruz's career. Minnesota Twins, 35 seasons (1991) The Twins made and won the World Series for the first time in 1987 then did it again in 1991, and have never so much as been in one since. It doesn’t help that when the team is worthy of the postseason, they often come up against the Yankees, a club that is 16-2 against them there since 2003 when they first faced off. The Twins might need to make it to meaningful October baseball in a season in which New York didn’t end up with a playoff spot in order to reverse this now 35-year-old trend. Colorado Rockies, 34 seasons The Rockies, unlike their expansion partner Marlins, have never won a World Series since they were brought into the league in 1993. They did make it to the 2007 Fall Classic, but were swept by the Red Sox. It might be awhile before they get another shot at ending this streak: the franchise has made the postseason just five times in 34 attempts, and has logged four-consecutive 100-loss seasons in a row, including 2025’s 119-loss campaign, which featured the third-most losses of the modern era among other historical indignities. Toronto Blue Jays, 33 seasons (1993) The Blue Jays won the 1992 and 1993 World Series, which were the only Fall Classics Toronto participated in until 2025. The Blue Jays have lost five American League Championship Series in their history — they joined MLB in 1977 — and have been swept in three AL Wild Card Series since 2020. Toronto did not get a chance at a World Series title again in 2026, as it never fully recovered from a slow start to the season, and finished in last place in the AL East, under .500 and half-a-game behind the Orioles. Tampa Bay Rays, 28 seasons The Rays were introduced to the league in 1998, and have never won a World Series. It’s not for a lack of opportunity, though: while the then-Devil Rays were famously an uncompetitive squad for the first decade of their existence, a name change in 2008 brought success. They lost in the ‘08 World Series to the Phillies and in 2020 to the Dodgers, with seven other postseason appearances besides those. The Rays made the postseason five years in a row, from 2019 through 2023, one of the longest streaks in league history. After missing the playoffs in 2024 and 2025, Tampa Bay is back in 2026, with a first-round bye after securing the AL's best record, awaiting the result of the Yankees-Red Sox Wild Card Series. Arizona Diamondbacks, 25 seasons (2001) Arizona was last in the World Series in 2023, and last won in 2001 against the Yankees. One championship in two pennants and seven postseason appearances is better than some other expansion teams have managed, but after missing the 2026 postseason by two games, the Diamondbacks have one gone 25 years without a title. Los Angeles Angels, 24 seasons (2002) Arte Moreno's ownership of the Angels ran from 2003 – the season after Los Angeles' lone World Series championship – through 2026. If the Angels win another title, it will be under another owner – possibly by a group led by Stan Kroenke, which has a deal in place to buy the team from Moreno. MLB Related StoriesMLB Wild-Card Power Rankings: The 8 Teams Who Kick Off The PlayoffsMLB Postseason Bracket, Schedule For Wild Card Round And World SeriesCleveland Guardians Make It Three Straight AL Central Titles Miami Marlins, 23 seasons (2003) The Marlins have two seasons with at least 90 wins, and in both of those Miami won the World Series. That puts them ahead of contemporary expansion teams like the Rays and Rockies, and even older ones like the Mariners, Padres and Brewers, but it's now been 23 years since the last time the Marlins won a championship. Chicago White Sox, 20 seasons (2005) The White Sox lost over 100 games in back-to-back-to-back seasons from 2023 through 2025, stretching Chicago's championship drought to two full decades. The White Sox are back in the postseason in 2026, however, giving them a chance at ending that streak. Chicago already became the first-ever team to reach the playoffs after consecutive 100-loss campaigns; anything is possible before the games are played.

articles.title: World Grand Prix Darts 2026: 'Double-in, double out' format, schedule, results, prize money & winners
articles.summary: BBC Sport's Ask Me Anything explains how Darts' World Grand Prix works ahead of the start of the 2026 tournament
articles.body:
The 2026 Darts World Grand Prix starts on Monday, 28 September and is one of the Professional Darts Corporation's major titles.

Unlike the rest of the sport's majors, the tournament uses a 'double in, double out' format.

The 32 players featuring are made up of the 16 best-ranked players from the PDC's Order of Merit, and the best 16 from the past 12 months via the Order of Merit who had not already qualified.

A total prize fund of £750,000 is up for grabs, with the winner earning £150,000.

Teenager and current world number one Luke Littler was the winner in 2025, cruising to a 6-1 victory over Luke Humphries in the final.

The 'double in, double out' darts format presents a big twist to the gameplay.

It means that a player must start all legs on a double, rather than on any scoring zone on the board.

The use of 'double in, double out' has been in use in the World Grand Prix since its inaugural year in 1998.

The format is in set play, with each set being the best of five legs.

The first round is a best-of-three-sets match, increasing to five sets in the second round.

The quarter-finals stay at the best of five sets, before an increase to nine sets in the semi-finals.

The final is a best-of-11 match, also described as a race to six sets.

(5) Jonny Clayton 2-1 Krzysztof Ratajski

(3) Gian van Veen v Dirk van Duijvenbode

Littler/Woodhouse v Nathan Aspinall (16)

Van Veen/Van Duijvenbode v Searle/O'Connor

The prize money for the whole tournament has increased to £750,000 this year, an increase of 25% from last year's £600,000.

The winner will take home £150,000 instead of the £120,000 jackpot 12 months ago. Barring the prize money given to players who lose in the first round, every other value has also increased.

Who has previously won the World Grand Prix?

Phil Taylor is the most successful player in World Grand Prix history, winning the tournament 11 times.

Michael van Gerwen is the next most successful player with six titles, with James Wade (twice) being the only other player to win it multiple times.

The World Grand Prix has produced six different winners in the last six years.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Week 3 Booms & Busts: The Lions just want to make managers happy this season
articles.summary: Scott Pianowski goes over who stepped up and who let you down for fantasy football in Week 3.
articles.body:
Fantasy football can be a stressful game for all of us. Injuries and underperformance, bad weather and curious calls. Sometimes it's a struggle merely to get through an NFL Sunday.

We all need some consistent things we can hang our hats on. And with that, we present to you the 2026 Detroit Lions . They just want to make fantasy managers happy.

The Lions are now three games deep into the NFL season, and every match has been a fantasy bonanza. First came a narrow win over the Saints in Week 1, a 31-30 overtime affair. Not much defense was played in Week 2, when the Bills outraced the Lions, 41-31.

And you can add Sunday's Week 3 result to the positive side of the ledger. Detroit held on for a 31-24 win over the Jets , with both teams pushing over their projected scoring total.

Jahmyr Gibbs was the main man for Detroit's offense, racking up 164 total yards and three scores (two rushing, one receiving). The other Detroit angles were a little muted — Amon-Ra St. Brown was held to four catches for 19 yards (thank goodness for touchdown deodorant) and Jameson Williams (4-49-0) and Sam LaPorta (3-44-0) were under expectation. Nonetheless, this is a consistent and bankable offense, and Jared Goff (8.4 YPA, 122.5 rating) is an efficient point guard. This offense will have a lot of right answers.

But the right answers also come on the other side of the ball, where Detroit's defense can't stop anything, especially against the pass. It's one thing when Josh Allen , arguably the league's best player, dominates the Lions a week ago (five total touchdowns). But the Lions also handed Tyler Shough a QB6 finish in Week 2, and Geno Smith was excellent Sunday (321 passing yards, three touchdowns, no turnovers). As we head to press, Smith is the QB2 in Week 3.

Smith brought some teammates along for the ride. Garrett Wilson (10-107-1, 13 targets) had the type of dominant game we know he's capable of, and Kenyon Sadiq (7-105-1) looks like the latest rookie tight end to hit the ground running. It's a shame Adonai Mitchell (finger) was scratched for this game, as he was likely to go off, too.

Breece Hall (55 total yards) left with a thigh injury and the Jets basically ditched the running game after that. Just as well, given the sorry nature of the injury-depleted Detroit secondary. Just pump some air into the football, and then throw it.

The only negative to Detroit's upcoming schedule is the Week 5 bye. Otherwise, we'll look forward to Detroit playing Carolina, Arizona and Green Bay in the next month.

The Lions look like fantasy football's ultimate carnival for 2026.

The Patriots have a Detroit game coming later this year, in the middle of November. Unfortunately for Drake Maye, the NFL won't let New England flex that game into Week 4. New England was stomped by the Jaguars on Sunday, 35-6, and Maye's poor start to the season continued. Maye threw two picks, lost a fumble, took three sacks and didn't get the Patriots into the end zone.

New England obviously misses top receiver A.J. Brown dearly; only journeyman Mack Hollins (6-87-0) was productive downfield Sunday. But a lot of Maye's negative plays this year have been a result of poor decisions or sloppy execution. It's a shocking turnaround for someone who came within an eyelash of winning the MVP last year.

Be gentle with New England fans in your life these days. They're starting to worry that Maye could be Mac Jones 2.0; the last No. 10 in Foxboro. Jones had a strong rookie year (10 wins, runner-up for Rookie of the Year) but quickly lost his mojo after that. He's currently the backup QB in San Francisco .

To be fair to Maye, his offense didn't help him much. TreVeyon Henderson (8-23-0) and Rhamondre Stevenson (7-22-0) went nowhere on the ground. New England also collected nine flags, a common theme throughout the league in a messy Week 3. We'd like to think that Maye, Mike Vrabel and Josh McDaniels can get this sorted out.

There's no letup in the schedule — the Patriots travel to Buffalo next week. If nothing else, Maye should get plenty of volume in that match as the Patriots look to keep up with Josh Allen's offense.

The Cincinnati carnival looks alive and well, as Joe Burrow led his offense to 27 points and watched the Cincinnati defense lose the game anyway. The Bengals , as usual, were tight in concentration — Chase Brown handled 15 touches and Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins combined for 15-188-2 on 19 targets. Maybe TE Mike Gesicki (3-37-1) can sneak into streaming consideration in October, but for the most part, this is a narrow target tree. The Bengals and Jaguars could light up the scoreboard in Week 4.

Jaylen Warren was the Pittsburgh beneficiary against Cincinnati, rolling up a splashy 176 total yards. It could have been even better — Warren didn't manage a touchdown and he had one long run called back by a negligible holding call. The passing game wasn't as fantasy-friendly; although Aaron Rodgers threw for 292 yards and three scores, he targeted 10 different teammates and no one had more than three catches. DK Metcalf (3-31-1) had one gift score on a blown coverage, but the other Pittsburgh scores went to Roman Wilson and Ben Skowronek . Even desperation TE play Pat Freiermuth (2-30-0) was outscored by Darnell Washington (3-67-0). The Pittsburgh at Cleveland game next week could turn into a rock fight.

Although I love the talent of Harold Fannin Jr. , I mostly passed on him this summer because of the Cleveland QB room. But Fannin overcame that messy situation last year, and maybe he can do it again. Fannin had a commanding nine targets in Sunday's win over Carolina, and he turned it into a 7-51-2 log, good enough for the top of the TE board. You'd like more downfield action, but if Fannin can control the target share and goal-line equity like this, he'll outkick his ADP for the second straight year.

Maybe it's charitable to put the Titans in the winner's section — midway through the third quarter, Tennessee had just one first down against an ordinary Giants defense. But the Titans moved the ball well after that point — they finished with 17 first downs — and at least Wan'Dale Robinson (7-57-1) and Tony Pollard (96 total yards) rewarded anyone desperate enough to start them. Cam Ward had just one pick and took just one sack, but he still looks like a confused young player. The Ravens and Texans come next.

In a previous world, Jameis Winston was the ultimate YOLO quarterback, a downfield daredevil who would throw his share of highlight passes and cover-your-eyes interceptions. The current Winston is a different animal, a buttoned-up veteran asked not to lose the game on his own. Winston had zero turnovers against the Titans but threw for just 118 yards on 5.4 YPA. It could be a long fall for Malik Nabers (5-26-0, six targets) and Isaiah Likely (2-13-0, five targets).

Seattle played a game against type at Washington, losing a 33-31 shootout. Somehow the Commanders turned a modest 258 total yards into 33 points — a defensive touchdown helped. The Seahawks ' passing game relied on Sam Darnold in catch-up mode (379 yards, four touchdowns, two picks), and of course no one can stop the amazing Jaxon Smith-Njigba (10-128-2). But everything the Seahawks tried on the ground failed miserably — Jadarian Price, Emanuel Wilson and George Holani combined for 39 yards on 17 carries. Nothing in the Seattle backfield looks playable as the Seahawks get ready for the Chargers in Week 4.

articles.title: At 19, Pincky Balhara lost three family members ahead of Asian Games debut; Now, she is only Indian to win multiple Kurash medals
articles.summary: Three family deaths in quick succession could have brought Pincky Balhara’s sporting journey to a halt.
articles.body: Three family deaths in quick succession could have brought Pincky Balhara’s sporting journey to a halt. Instead, the Delhi athlete carried her grief into the competition arena, turned her father’s dream into motivation and went on to win an Asian Games medal.Eight years after her historic silver at the 2018 Jakarta Asian Games, Balhara returned to the continental podium on Monday, winning bronze in the women’s -78kg Kurash event at the 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Games. The bronze is Balhara’s second Asian Games medal in Kurash, following her silver in the women’s -52kg category in Jakarta. She has now become the only Indian athlete to win multiple Asian Games medals in Kurash.What is Kurash?Kurash is a traditional Central Asian martial art that originated in the region and is particularly associated with Uzbekistan. It made its Asian Games debut at the 2018 Jakarta Games. The basic objective is simple: throw the opponent onto their back while remaining in a standing position. Unlike judo or Brazilian jiu-jitsu, Kurash does not involve prolonged ground fighting.From judo mats to KurashBorn on October 20, 1998, in Neb Sarai, Delhi, Balhara began training in judo when she was nine. Her maternal uncle, Samundar Tokas, a former judoka and coach, played a major role in her early development.She quickly established herself in judo, winning gold at the 2018 Asian Junior Judo Championships. But she missed out on India's judo squad for the 2018 Jakarta Asian Games. That disappointment opened another door.With Kurash making its Asian Games debut in Jakarta, Balhara entered the trials. The sport, which shares similarities with judo but is contested entirely from a standing position, offered her another route to the continental stage. She made the team and was soon heading to Jakarta.Three deaths changed everythingBut just weeks before the Games, Balhara's life was shattered. She lost her cousin brother first, followed by her father, who died of a heart attack, and then her grandfather. The three deaths came in quick succession, leaving the teenager struggling to cope with the loss.Her father had been particularly excited about her selection for the Asian Games. After his death, Balhara initially did not want to compete. Her uncle, however, pushed her to continue, reminding her of her father's hopes for her career.She returned to training while dealing with grief and also had to make the weight for her 52kg category. She later recalled going to the gym at night because she feared people would judge her for returning to training so soon after her father's death.Balhara eventually made it to the 2018 Asian Games and produced a remarkable run. At just 19, she reached the women's -52kg Kurash final, becoming one of India's first Asian Games medallists in the sport. She eventually lost to Uzbekistan's Gulnor Sulaymanova and settled for silver.Balhara later recalled her father's prediction before the Games: that she would win silver rather than gold. When she finished second, she remembered his words. At Aichi-Nagoya, Balhara began her campaign with a 3-0 quarterfinal victory over South Korea's Garam Lim, securing her place in the semifinals and guaranteeing India another Kurash medal.She then faced South Korea's Sumin Mo in the last four. Mo won 5-0, sending Balhara into the bronze-medal position.Eight years after her first Asian Games medal, Balhara was back on the podium.Pincky Balhara's Asian Games recordYearGamesCategoryResult2018JakartaWomen's -52kg🥈 Silver2022HangzhouWomen's KurashQuarterfinal2026Aichi-NagoyaWomen's -78kg🥉 BronzeStay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Los dos 'fichajes' que lo cambian todo en el Valencia
articles.standfirst: Casino Gran Madrid saca al conjunto 'che' del descenso tras las llegadas de Javier Aguirre y Braulio Vázquez
articles.summary: Casino Gran Madrid saca al conjunto 'che' del descenso tras las llegadas de Javier Aguirre y Braulio Vázquez
articles.body: Hay veces que los mejores fichajes no se hacen para actuar sobre el terreno de juego. Después de un inicio de temporada bastante convulso, el Valencia ha movido ficha y ha incorporado a Javier Aguirre para ocupar el banquillo y a Braulio Vázquez para liderar la dirección deportiva. Dos movimientos que han cambiado, de un plumazo, la percepción alrededor del conjunto 'che' y que pretenden darle un nuevo rumbo después de un arranque que dejó al equipo en una situación delicada. Los apenas cuatro puntos sumados en las siete primeras jornadas se llevaron por delante a Carlos Corberán y provocaron que el Valencia llegara al primer parón de selecciones de la temporada en puestos de descenso junto a Málaga y Elche. Ahora, sin embargo, la llegada de Aguirre y Braulio ha modificado los pronósticos. Casino Gran Madrid asigna al Valencia una cuota de 3.5 para descender a Segunda, por encima de la que presentan equipos que actualmente están fuera de la zona roja de la tabla como Racing (2.5) o Levante (2.85). Las apuestas deportivas empiezan a reflejar así la confianza generada por el cambio de rumbo en Mestalla. Ahora le toca al Valencia demostrar sobre el terreno de juego que esa nueva percepción tiene fundamento. Aguirre está aprovechando este parón para realizar una especie de 'mini' pretemporada y preparar a conciencia su estreno, que llegará ante el Racing en El Sardinero. El conjunto 'che' tendrá una primera oportunidad para empezar a dejar atrás las dudas de las primeras jornadas y convertir las llegadas de su nuevo entrenador y director deportivo en algo más que un cambio de imagen. Las mejores casas de apuestas reflejan precisamente la igualdad que se espera en ese primer examen. Tonybet paga a 2.22 la victoria del Racing, mientras que el empate cotiza a 3.75 y el triunfo del Valencia alcanza una cuota de 2.83. Unas cifras que dejan claro que el conjunto valencianista tendrá que demostrar desde el primer día que la llegada de Aguirre puede convertirse en el punto de inflexión que necesitaba para comenzar a alejarse de la zona peligrosa. El Valencia ya ha hecho sus dos grandes movimientos fuera del césped. Javier Aguirre y Braulio Vázquez llegan con la misión de cambiar la dinámica de un equipo que apenas había sumado cuatro puntos en siete jornadas y que necesita reaccionar cuanto antes. El primer capítulo de esta nueva etapa se escribirá en El Sardinero, donde los 'che' podrán comprobar si sus dos nuevos 'fichajes' han sido capaces de cambiar algo más que los pronósticos.

articles.title: Cuatro muertos y 12 desaparecidos en una montaña de Nepal por una avalancha
articles.standfirst: Todas las víctimas mortales y los desaparecidos son ciudadanos nepalíes que se encontraban en el campamento base preparándose para la llegada de clientes extranjeros
articles.summary: Todas las víctimas mortales y los desaparecidos son ciudadanos nepalíes que se encontraban en el campamento base preparándose para la llegada de clientes extranjeros
articles.body: Equipos de rescate buscaban el lunes a una docena de personas arrastradas por una avalancha que mató al menos a cuatro individuos en una montaña nepalí durante condiciones meteorológicas adversas. Los rescatistas de la Asociación Nacional de Guías de Montaña de Nepal, que lidera las operaciones, informaron que recuperaron dos cuerpos más el lunes, sumándose a los dos hallados el domingo. Hay doce personas desaparecidas. Ocho experimentados guías de montaña de la asociación aprovecharon la mejora del tiempo para excavar en la nieve que había cubierto las tiendas de campaña en el campamento base. Diez personas fueron rescatadas del monte Himlung, una cima de 7.126 metros situada en el centro-norte de Nepal, después de que la avalancha golpeara la zona el domingo. Todas las víctimas mortales y los desaparecidos eran ciudadanos nepalíes. Se encontraban en el campamento base preparándose para la llegada de clientes extranjeros que escalarían la cima durante la temporada de otoño —iniciada este mes— cuando fueron arrastrados por el alud. Helicópteros trasladaron los cuerpos al aeropuerto de Katmandú. Familiares y amigos presentes en la morgue del hospital no hicieron declaraciones. Las inundaciones y los deslizamientos de tierra en el distrito de Manang, donde se encuentra la montaña, fueron provocados por fuertes lluvias, según informó la oficina administrativa del distrito. Se habían emitido alertas por condiciones meteorológicas adversas en toda la nación del Himalaya. La agencia de gestión de desastres de Nepal comunicó que otras 21 personas han fallecido y cinco más permanecen desaparecidas en diferentes partes del país entre el jueves y el domingo. Nepal se está recuperando de unas inundaciones devastadoras ocurridas en agosto, que arrasaron varias aldeas y dejaron más de 1.400 muertos y cerca de 6.000 desaparecidos.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indian distance runner Gulveer Singh continued his impressive campaign at the Asian Games 2026, winning his second silver medal in Japan with a personal best performance in the men's 1500m final on Monday.Gulveer clocked 3:36.72 to finish second behind Japan's Kazuto Iizawa, who clinched gold, while another Japanese runner, Nagiya Mori, took bronze in 3:37.92. India's other finalist, Yoonus Shah, finished ninth with a time of 3:43.88.The silver added to Gulveer's medal collection at the ongoing Games, having already secured a second-place finish in the men's 10,000m. His latest podium finish also provided a bright spot for Indian athletics on a day when defending champion Avinash Sable missed out on a medal in the 3000m steeplechase.Gulveer's double silver underlined his consistency across two demanding distance events, as he improved his personal best in the 1500m to finish among the leading runners in the field.Asian Games Full Coverage | Medal Tally | ScheduleVithya breaks PT Usha's record with 400m hurdles bronzeEarlier, Vithya Ramraj delivered a historic performance in the women's 400m hurdles, winning bronze with a personal best of 54.75 seconds and breaking a national record that had stood for more than four decades.The 28-year-old from Coimbatore finished behind UAE's Mariam Kareem, who won gold in a Games-record 54.31 seconds, and Kazakhstan's Adelina Zems, who took silver in a personal best of 54.58.Vithya bettered the 55.42 seconds recorded by legendary Indian athlete PT Usha at the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics. It was her second medal at the Games, following silver in the 4x400m mixed relay.India's Anu Raghavan finished fifth in the final with a personal best of 55.88 seconds.Sable's title defence ends in disappointmentThe day's biggest setback for India came in the men's 3000m steeplechase, where defending champion and Games record holder Avinash Sable finished fourth despite clocking a season-best 8:21.67.The 32-year-old two-time Olympian from Maharashtra, who has been troubled by injuries, finished 4.31 seconds behind Japan's Ryuji Miura, who won gold in a Games-record 8:17.36. Miura's compatriot Ryoma Aoki claimed silver in a personal best of 8:17.60, while Qatar's Zakaria Elahlaami took bronze in 8:18.13.Sable's failure to defend his title was a major disappointment for India, particularly after he had established himself as one of the country's leading distance runners.There was further frustration in the women's discus throw, where Commonwealth Games bronze medallist Seema Kaliramna finished fourth despite recording a personal best of 59.88m in her fifth attempt. articles.title: Athletes criticise organisational, logistical mishaps at ‘sad’ Asian Games
articles.summary: Athletes transported to the wrong venues, three matches in 18 hours and an accommodation crisis add to organisers’ woes.
articles.body:
Repeated incidents of organisational failure at the Asian Games have left athletes frustrated, exhausted and disappointed as rain-delayed matches became the latest headache for host nation Japan.

A glitzy opening ceremony did little to overshadow the growing accommodation crisis , logistical gaffes and scheduling issues that have headlined the Games, which opened on September 19 in Aichi-Nagoya.

India’s multiple-Olympic medallist PV Sindhu lamented a badminton schedule that saw her play three matches within 18 hours.

“Three matches in 18 hours. Back at 3am, out again at 8:30am. It took a toll,” Sindhu wrote on social media after her quarterfinal exit on Sunday.

Pakistan’s volleyball team was mistakenly taken to the wrong gymnasium an hour before the start of its preliminary round match, forcing its members to change into their kits on the bus and leaving them without enough time for a warm-up.

“Japan has destroyed the dignity and discipline of the Asian Games,” men’s captain Murad Jehan wrote in a now-deleted video on his Instagram account as the team travelled to their match against Uzbekistan, which they won 3-0. “Really disappointing situation.”

He said athletes would often return from training to find their hotel restaurant closed, leaving them unable to eat. “This situation at Asian Games is not acceptable.”

The South Korean men’s basketball team faced a similar incident when they missed a light practice session hours before their final after their shuttle bus did not show up on time. Team officials said they received no explanation.

It was a repeat of what the men’s football team faced when the bus did not arrive at the team’s hotel. A day earlier, the bus took the athletes to a baseball ground instead of the Mizuho Rugby Stadium, causing a 30-minute delay.

On Monday, persistent rain became the organisers’ latest headache when it disrupted several competitions, including tennis, surfing and cricket.

Both the men’s cricket quarterfinals between Pakistan-Hong Kong and India-Afghanistan were washed out after the playing field was drenched at Korogi Athletic Park on the outskirts of Nagoya.

With no contingency built into the schedule for rained-off matches, Pakistan and India advanced to the semifinals of the T20 tournament by virtue of their higher rankings.

It was a bitter pill for Afghanistan, who saw the gold medal go to India due to the rankings rule three years ago when their Hangzhou Games final was abandoned due to rain.

“The rain started yesterday, so hard luck for us,” Afghanistan opener Mohammed Akram said.

“We would have been happy to play here with India. Our players are in form.

“But unfortunately the rain has ruined everything.”

Typhoon Surigae lashed southern Japan’s Okinawa prefecture on Monday and was projected to track northeast towards central Japan and the Tokyo region by midweek, raising the prospect of strong winds and heavy rain further disrupting the Games.

Typhoon Dujuan hit the Games early in week one, causing equestrian events in Tokyo to be suspended although most competitions were unaffected.

The continental sporting showpiece is mainly based in the city of Nagoya and Aichi prefecture, but Tokyo is also hosting diving events while Osaka is hosting football matches.

The rain saw several tennis matches scrapped on Sunday and caused match delays on Monday.

Fans hoping to catch Filipino headliner Alex Eala’s opening match against Thai opponent Patcharin Cheapchandej were repeatedly frustrated at the Higashiyama Park Tennis Centre.

Eala, the women’s top seed, had her match shifted off centre court amid the scheduling logjam and wrapped it up in 55 minutes with a 6-1, 6-0 win over Patcharin.

Poor wave conditions saw the surfing called off early at the Long Beach venue southeast of Nagoya with medal finals having already been pushed to Tuesday.

India’s Kishore Kumar Anbarasu was able to complete his heat before it was abandoned, beating China’s Ma Wensong to make it into the quarterfinals on the sport’s Asian Games debut.

“It was not the easiest conditions. It was very hard to find the good waves,” Anbarasu said.

Organisers on Saturday apologised for logistical glitches at the Games that left thousands of athletes with cramped housing conditions and undersized beds that forced several countries to house their athletes elsewhere.

Satoshi Murate, secretary-general of the local organising committee, said a late influx of about 2,000 additional athletes and officials had stretched resources.

“There have been mistakes in accommodation and transport for various reasons,” Murate said.

“Whatever the cause, AINAGOC [the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games and Asian Para Games Organising Committee] is responsible for providing the service, and I frankly apologise for the mistakes.

“Our staff work every day to identify the causes of each mistake and make sure they don’t happen again. I think you can see that accommodation and transport have improved greatly compared with the early days.”

Organisers chose not to build a traditional athletes village in a bid to save money. Competitors instead are staying in hotels, temporary wooden units and on a cruise ship.

India’s multiple badminton medallist HS Prannoy said that made for a disappointing experience.

“It was sad,” the 34-year-old, who won team bronze, said in a YouTube video published by the Badminton Association of India.

“It never felt like we were playing in an Asian Games, to be honest.”

articles.title: Philadelphia Flyers and Trevor Zegras jersey controversy: What are the NHL’s new jersey-tucking rules, penalty details and protest all about
articles.summary: Trevor Zegras' unusual jersey penalty has stirred up significant discussions in the NHL, prompting the Philadelphia Flyers to support him with a striking warmup protest against revived jersey-tucking rules ahead of the 2026-27 season.
articles.body: An odd preseason penalty on Trevor Zegras has become one of the most talked-about equipment stories in the NHL heading into the 2026-27 regular season for the Philadelphia Flyers. Officials ruled Zegras' jersey was tucked into his pants at the start of a shift against the Boston Bruins, making him the first player in years to receive a penalty for the infraction.The incident took off fast as the practice of tucking a jersey has been around the NHL for a long time, even by prominent players in the past. The Fliers had another chapter added to their story against the Washington Capitals when several players showed up for warmups with their jerseys tucked in, apparently in support of Zegras and calling attention to the league's renewed enforcement of equipment rules.Philadelphia Flyers players support Trevor Zegras with jersey protestThe Philadelphia Flyers made their position known ahead of their preseason finale against the Washington Capitals on September 26. Two days after Zegras was penalized for the same way of wearing his jersey during a game against the Boston Bruins, most of the team took the ice for warmups with their jersey tucked into their pants.Captain Sean Couturier and alternate captains Travis Konecny and Travis Sanheim were among players seen with tucked jerseys during warmups, along with Rasmus Ristolainen, Porter Martone, Alex Bump, Cam York and Jamie Drysdale.Trevor Zegras penalty sparks unusual NHL rule controversyTrevor Zegras served two minutes for delay of game for “improperly wearing equipment” in the Philadelphia Flyers’ 2-0 preseason win over the Boston Bruins on Sept. 24. Zegras had already been warned about the tucked jersey, but the penalty came at 9:51 of the second period.The NHL’s enforcement is predicated on existing equipment rules, not a new, stand-alone jersey-tucking rule. Rule 12.1 states that the penalty for illegal equipment is a warning if the problem is not corrected. Rule 9.5 states that protective equipment must be worn under the uniform.Philadelphia Flyers keep protest to preseason warmupsThe Philadelphia Flyers’ warm-up display came in response to Zegras’ social media comments about the controversy. He shared pictures of himself with his jersey tucked in from his youth hockey days and even referenced the infamous NFL “Tuck Rule” controversy involving Tom Brady.The NHL has signaled it will be paying more attention to equipment compliance, and now players will have to ensure their jerseys stay untucked when they begin shifts. articles.summary: Defending champions India ended their Asian Games group campaign in style, thrashing Bangladesh 10-0 in a rain-hit match on Monday.
articles.body: Defending champions India ended their Asian Games group campaign in style, thrashing Bangladesh 10-0 in a rain-hit match on Monday.Captain Harmanpreet Singh scored a hat-trick as India finished at the top of Pool A. They will now face arch-rivals Pakistan in the semi-final on October 1.The other semi-final will see Malaysia take on South Korea.India were unbeaten in the group stage, beating Indonesia, Sri Lanka, Japan, South Korea and Bangladesh. Mandeep Singh was blocked inside the circle, resulting in a penalty corner.Jugraj Singh's drag-flick hit the foot of a defender on the post, and India were awarded a penalty stroke. Jugraj made no mistake to make it 2-0.Five minutes later, Harmanpreet added another. Mandeep created the opening for a penalty corner, and Harmanpreet's powerful flick beat the Bangladesh defence.India went into half-time 3-0 ahead.India run riot after the breakIndia increased the pressure after the restart.In the 32nd minute, Dilpreet Singh and Sukhjeet Singh combined with quick passes to beat the Bangladesh defence. Sukhjeet then found the open goal to make it 4-0.Harmanpreet struck again in the 40th minute after Vivek Sagar Prasad won a penalty corner.Shilanand Lakra then scored twice in the 44th and 45th minutes as India moved 7-0 ahead.The goals continued to come in the final quarter, with India completing a 10-0 win.Harmanpreet scored three times, while Abhishek scored three goals, and Jugraj Singh, Sukhjeet Singh, Shilanand Lakra and Sanjay also found the net. articles.body: NEW DELHI: India enjoyed another medal-rich day at the Asian Games 2026 on Monday, winning eight medals across athletics, shooting and kurash while also securing more medals in boxing. Yet the haul came with a familiar mix of celebration and disappointment, as several Indian athletes came agonisingly close to the podium.The eight medals included four silver and four bronze, with Yashvir Singh and Rohit Yadav winning a javelin double, Murali Sreeshankar taking long jump silver, Gulveer Singh adding his second silver of the Games and Esha Singh claiming silver in the women's 25m pistol. Vithya Ramraj, Parul Chaudhary and Pincky Balhara completed the day's bronze-medal haul.India also secured at least three more medals in boxing as three boxers — Lovlina Borgohain, Priya and Kapil Pokhariya — confirmed podium finishes by winning their respective quarterfinals.Asian Games Full Coverage | Medal Tally | ScheduleJavelin double, Gulveer's second silver headline athletics haulIn the absence of defending champion Neeraj Chopra, Yashvir Singh and Rohit Yadav ensured India still finished with two athletes on the men's javelin podium.Yashvir produced a personal best of 85.72m to win silver, while Rohit took bronze with 84.35m. Sri Lanka's Rumesh Pathirage won gold with 88.55m.Yashvir had started strongly with 83.56m and briefly led the competition, while Rohit moved to the top with 84.35m. Pathirage eventually took control with 88.33m before improving further in his final attempt.Gulveer, meanwhile, continued his outstanding campaign by winning his second silver medal. After finishing runner-up in the 10,000m, he clocked a personal best of 3:36.72 in the 1500m final. Japan's Kazuto Iizawa won gold, while compatriot Nagiya Mori took bronze. India's Yoonus Shah finished ninth.ALSO READ: India win 8 medals but remain outside top 10 as gold continues to eludeSreeshankar wins silver despite injuryMurali Sreeshankar endured a tense finish to win silver in the men's long jump.The Indian produced a best effort of 8.07m, but injured himself during his fourth attempt and could not take either of his final two jumps. Having already moved into silver-medal position, Sreeshankar could only watch as his rivals tried to overtake his mark. None succeeded.China's Yuhao Shi won gold with 8.17m, while Uzbekistan's Anvar Anvarov took bronze with 8.06m. India's Solomon David finished seventh with 7.70m.There were also bronze medals for Parul Chaudhary and Vithya Ramraj. Parul clocked 15:14.61 to finish third in the women's 5000m, adding another bronze after her steeplechase medal.Vithya, meanwhile, set a personal best of 54.75 seconds to win bronze in the 400m hurdles and break PT Usha's more than four-decade-old national record. Anu Raghavan finished fifth with a personal best of 55.88 seconds.Esha fights through shoot-offs, Balhara adds kurash bronzeEsha Singh had to negotiate multiple shoot-offs before securing silver in the women's 25m pistol.The world No. 1 finished with 38 hits, the same score as China's Xiao Jiaruixuan. Xiao eventually won the gold after the deciding shoot-off, leaving Esha with silver.Esha's route to the podium included three shoot-offs against South Korea's Kim Hyon Suk during the elimination stages before she secured her place in the medal positions.Pincky Balhara also added a bronze in women's -78kg kurash. She beat South Korea's Garam Lim in the quarterfinal before losing 0-5 to another South Korean, Sumin Mo, in the semifinals.It was Balhara's second Asian Games medal, eight years after her silver at Jakarta 2018.Boxing guarantees three more medalsIndia's medal count will rise further after three boxers won their quarterfinal bouts.Lovlina Borgohain defeated South Korea's Seong Suyeon in the women's 75kg quarterfinal to confirm a medal. Priya also advanced to the podium by beating Tajikistan's Mijgona Samadova in the women's 60kg quarterfinal.Kapil Pokhariya completed the boxing trio, defeating South Korea's Kim Gichae in the men's 90kg quarterfinal.The three victories mean India is guaranteed at least three more boxing medals, although their colour will be determined by their semifinal and final results.Hockey sets up blockbuster Pakistan semifinalThe defending champions produced one of their most emphatic performances of the Games, crushing Bangladesh 10-0 in their final Pool A match.Captain Harmanpreet Singh scored a hat-trick, while Abhishek struck three times. Jugraj Singh, Sukhjeet Singh, Shilanand Lakra, Sanjay and Mandeep Singh also got on the scoresheet.India finished top of Pool A with five wins from five matches and a +45 goal difference. The result sets up a blockbuster semifinal against arch-rivals Pakistan on October 1. Malaysia and South Korea will contest the other semifinal.More near misses on a busy dayNot everything went India's way. Defending champion and Games record holder Avinash Sable finished fourth in the men's 3000m steeplechase despite producing a season-best 8:21.67. Japan's Ryuji Miura won gold in a Games record 8:17.36.Seema Kaliramna also missed the women's discus podium by a narrow margin, finishing fourth with a personal-best 59.88m. All three medal winners crossed 60m. India also finished fourth in the women's 4x100m relay.Santhosh Kumar Tamilarasan was seventh in the men's 400m hurdles, while India's women's 25m pistol team of Manu Bhaker, Esha Singh and Rahi Sarnobat finished fifth.Elsewhere, India qualified for the men's 4x400m relay final and mixed 4x100m relay final, while Pooja reached the women's 800m final. Squash produced a clean sweep of sorts, with India's women's team beating Japan and China and the men's side defeating China and South Korea.Rain also affected the men's cricket quarterfinal against Afghanistan, which was abandoned, with India advancing to the semifinal by virtue of higher seeding.After the day's eight medals, India stood on 45 medals — four gold, 20 silver and 21 bronze. The medal haul continued to grow, but the country's gold tally remained unchanged, leaving India 12th in the standings.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Dwayne Johnson’s daughters grew up with The Rock as their father, offering a glimpse into the WWE icon’s family life away from Hollywood, fame and the wrestling spotlight
articles.summary: Explore the family life of Dwayne \"The Rock\" Johnson away from the WWE and Hollywood glare, focusing on his three daughters and their unique upbringing.
articles.body: Dwayne “The Rock” Johnson has built a career spanning WWE, blockbuster movies, business ventures and global entertainment over decades. But away from his professional commitments, fatherhood has been an important part of his personal life. His three daughters have lived through different phases of his career as they grew up in a household tied to wrestling and Hollywood.He has a daughter, Simone Alexandra Johnson, from his former marriage to Dany Garcia. He has two youngest daughters, Jasmine Lia Johnson and Tiana Gia Johnson, with his wife, Lauren Hashian. At times, the three sisters have accompanied their father to public events, and Johnson has spoken about how having girls has impacted his approach to family life.Dwayne Johnson’s daughters Simone, Jasmine and Tiana are growing up around his Hollywood and WWE legacyJohnson became a dad for the first time when Simone arrived in August 2001. Years later, he welcomed Jasmine in December 2015 and Tiana in April 2018. So the three daughters represent the different stages of Johnson's journey from professional wrestling star to one of Hollywood's most recognizable actors.Simone, especially, finds the WWE tie-in meaningful. Johnson’s own wrestling career helped establish the family name in sports entertainment, following in the footsteps of her grandfather, Rocky Johnson, and great-grandfather, Peter Maivia. Simone later pursued wrestling herself, creating a direct link between the family’s previous generations and her own career.For Jasmine and Tiana, childhood has unfolded largely away from the professional wrestling spotlight. But Johnson has still offered occasional glimpses into their family moments, from celebrations to outings to milestones. Despite his busy career, he has spoken publicly about how important it is to spend quality time with his daughters.Simone Alexandra Johnson was born Aug. 14, 2001, to Johnson and Dany Garcia. Eventually, she followed in her family's footsteps in wrestling and signed with WWE in 2020, beginning training at the WWE Performance Center in Orlando, Florida.In 2022, Simone made her WWE television debut under the name Ava Raine. Wrestling gave her a chance to carve out her own identity in the industry, while still being attached to a family with deep WWE roots.Dwayne Johnson’s daughters Simone, Jasmine and Tiana share family spotlightWhile Simone has taken a professional route connected to wrestling, Jasmine Lia Johnson and Tiana Gia Johnson have primarily grown up away from the professional entertainment business. Johnson and Lauren Hashian have had family moments with their younger daughters from time to time.Jasmine was born on 16th December 2015. Johnson has been candid about their relationship and given glimpses of movie nights, family celebrations and everyday life. She also joined her father at his Hollywood Walk of Fame ceremony when she was a little girl.Tiana Gia Johnson was born April 17, 2018. Johnson has written about some of her childhood memories, including her birthdays and her father having fun with her. His public posts have often exposed a different side to the larger-than-life persona of The Rock.Jasmine and Tiana had a famous dad growing up, but Johnson has tended to depict their home life through mundane family moments, as opposed to his professional achievements. The family’s public outings have been highlighted by birthday parties, games, celebrations and time spent together.Johnson also has a different view of his public persona since becoming a father. His remarks about raising daughters have often focused on listening, patience and being present. articles.title: Mike Matheson faces NHL discipline after Montreal Canadiens defenseman’s preseason attack on Ridly Greig: What happened during the Montreal Canadiens-Ottawa Senators game
articles.summary: Discover the details of the altercation between Mike Matheson and Ridly Greig during the Montreal Canadiens-Ottawa Senators preseason game, and learn about Matheson's $5,000 fine by the NHL for roughing.
articles.body: The Montreal Canadiens and Ottawa Senators met in preseason, and there was a significant disciplinary development following an altercation involving Mike Matheson and Ridley Greig. The incident took place Saturday, Sept. 26, in the second period at Montreal’s Bell Center.The NHL Department of Player Safety reviewed the sequence and made its decision Sunday. Matheson was fined $5,000, the maximum allowable under the Collective Bargaining Agreement, for roughing Greig. Matheson will not sit out any games because of the financial penalty for the incident.Mike Matheson faces discipline after attack on Ridly GreigThe play took place at 10:43 of the second period when Greig and Matheson were fighting in front of the Montreal net. Sources say Greig reached out to Matheson during the net-front battle, and the Montreal defenseman threw a punch back.The two players then moved toward the ice, and Matheson continued the exchange. Officialsintervened after the confrontation became heated, with both players drawing two-minute roughing penalties during the game.The NHL later assessed an additional $5,000 fine for roughing in Matheson’s actions. The money will go to the Players’ Emergency Assistance Fund, the league said.Discipline detailInformationPlayerMike MathesonTeamMontreal CanadiensOpposing playerRidly GreigInfractionRoughingFine$5,000SuspensionNoneIncident time10:43 of second periodFund receiving finePlayers’ Emergency Assistance FundRidly Greig draws attention during preseason clashMatheson engaged in the net-front battle with the Ottawa Senators forward Ridly Greig. The exchange quickly became one of the most talked-about moments from the preseason meeting between the two Atlantic Division clubs.Greig and Matheson were battling for position around the Montreal net before the fight broke out, reports say. Matheson reacted after going down and hit Greig before more contact ensued on the ice.Greig also received a minor for roughing in the game, but the announced supplementary discipline from the NHL was for Matheson. The league’s official announcement of the $5,000 fine identified Matheson as the only player involved.Matheson avoids suspension before regular seasonNHL ruling clears Matheson to play in Montreal Canadiens’ regular-season opener. The fine is the maximum allowable under the current collective agreement, but does not include a game suspension.That difference matters for Montreal, as the preseason incident happened just days before the Canadiens start their regular-season schedule. Sportsnet has reported that Montreal will open its season on Sept. 29 versus the Toronto Maple Leafs and Ottawa will open its regular season against the same opponent on Oct. 3.Montreal Canadiens await fallout from NHL decisionThe $5,000 fine brings a clear end to the league’s examination of the Matheson-Greig confrontation. NHL Player Safety determined that the play was a case of roughing and issued the maximum fine allowable under the CBA, rather than a suspension.The decision also keeps the focus on how preseason physicality can have disciplinary ramifications even without a suspension. Matheson’s case is a reminder that the NHL can still levy supplemental discipline even after an on-ice penalty has already been called.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Shaili Singh's long jump mark wrongly measured by Asian Games officials, will move CAS: AFI
articles.summary: The Athletics Federation of India (AFI) will approach the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) over the measurement of Shaili Singh's fourth attempt in
articles.body: The Athletics Federation of India (AFI) will approach the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) over the measurement of Shaili Singh's fourth attempt in the women's long jump at the Asian Games.The AFI claims that officials measured the jump from a shorter mark, which cost Shaili a medal.Shaili finishes fourthShaili finished fourth with a best jump of 6.42m on Sunday. India's Ancy Sojan won silver with 6.53m, while China's Huang Yingying took gold with 6.55m on her final attempt.The controversy centres on Shaili's fourth attempt, which was officially measured at 6.41m.According to Shaili's mentor and legendary long jumper Anju Bobby George, the measurement was taken from the wrong mark."We saw her jump was clearly ahead of the gold-winning mark. Initially, the official near the landing pit pointed to Shaili's leg mark for the measurement."But later another official who was standing far behind came and pointed to a mark which was far shorter from board," Anju told PTI.'The measurement should have been done' differentlyAnju said the measurement was ultimately taken from the mark pointed out by the official who was standing farther away from the landing pit."They took the measurement at the mark pointed by the official who was standing far behind. The measurement should have been done on the mark pointed by the official nearest to the landing pit," said Anju, who won a long jump bronze in the 2003 World Championships.Shaili also lodged a protest after the attempt, and the officials showed videos of the jump to the Indian team.Indian team unhappy with video reviewAnju said the officials first showed them a front-view video, which the team felt could not establish where Shaili had landed."We were called after the event, and the officials showed a front view video to us, which does not mean anything. How would you know where Shaili landed from a front view? We demanded a side view video, which they said was not with them."Later, we made an appeal to the jury. The jury later sent their decision saying that they have looked into the side view videos also, and the earlier decision stands.AFI to take matter to CASAnju, who is also the senior vice president of the AFI, said the federation believes Shaili was denied a medal because of the measurement."It's an injustice to Shaili. She could have even won gold if the correct measurement was made. So, we are going to CAS," Anju, also the senior vice president of the AFI, said.Another AFI top official also confirmed to PTI that the body is moving the Lausanne-based CAS against official decision.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: La verdad tras los audios de Juanjo Gutiérrez a Leal y Guerrero: “Espero que nos animéis desde el sofá”
articles.standfirst: El seleccionador nacional envió una nota de voz en tono irónico a los jugadores tras su gesto en el FIP Platinum de Lyon, un contenido privado que posteriormente fue difundido en redes sociales
articles.summary: El seleccionador nacional envió una nota de voz en tono irónico a los jugadores tras su gesto en el FIP Platinum de Lyon, un contenido privado que posteriormente fue difundido en redes sociales
articles.body: Tras la publicación de la convocatoria de la selección española de pádel para el Mundial de Doha, en la que no resultaron incluidos Fran Guerrero ni Javi Leal, la pareja andaluza conquistó el FIP Platinum de Lyon frente a Franco Stupaczuk y Jon Sanz. Durante la celebración, ambos jugadores realizaron el gesto de una llamada telefónica ante las cámaras de la retransmisión. Tras este hecho, el seleccionador nacional, Juanjo Gutiérrez, remitió un mensaje de voz privado por WhatsApp a los dos deportistas, cuyo contenido ha circulado en redes sociales. MARCA ha tenido acceso al contexto en el que se produjeron los hechos y a las valoraciones de las partes implicadas. En la nota de voz, una a cada uno, Gutiérrez empleó un tono distendido e irónico para referirse tanto a la categoría del torneo como a la celebración de los jugadores: “Os he quitado presión el jueves. Espero que valoréis mi aportación y que me hagáis llegar un porcentaje del torneo. Si seguís ganando FIP, os juro que vais al Europeo”, expresó el técnico en relación con el título obtenido. En el mismo mensaje, contestó al gesto con otro 'palo': “Espero que nos animéis desde el sofá. Os he regalado una semana. Es que no se valora”, concluyendo la comunicación con palabras de felicitación: “Me alegro mucho por el torneo, que hayáis ganado y que me hayáis tirado el 'dardito'. Nos vemos en Rotterdam”. La difusión pública de este audio privado generó diversos comentarios en redes sociales al interpretarse el mensaje fuera del marco de confianza en el que fue enviado. Tal y como ha podido conocer este medio, desde el entorno de Leal y Guerrero se señala que, pudiendo no estar de acuerdo, los jugadores acatan la decisión técnica de la convocatoria oficial. Asimismo, condenan la divulgación del material de audio: “Forman parte de una conversación privada entre personas que tienen la confianza suficiente para expresarse en esos términos. Analizarlos de manera aislada puede dar lugar a interpretaciones que no se corresponden con la realidad ni con la intención con la que fueron enviados”. El equipo de representación de los deportistas afirma categóricamente que la difusión del archivo no procedió de los jugadores ni de sus entornos directos. A este respecto, el propio Javi Leal se manifestó en la red social X para desmentir las acusaciones de filtración: “En ningún momento se los pasamos a nadie”. Por su parte, la Federación Española de Pádel (FEP) ha optado por no emitir un comunicado oficial tras la reunión mantenida entre su presidente, Javier Rodríguez Piris, el seleccionador Juanjo Gutiérrez y el director de comunicación, Nacho Palencia. Fuentes federativas encuadran lo sucedido en un intercambio privado fuera de contexto que no altera la relación profesional entre el técnico y los internacionales, a quienes la institución considera activos de relevancia para el presente y futuro del pádel nacional. Además, confían en la honorabilidad de los tres, señalando que no saben cómo han podido hacerse públicos los mensajes.

articles.title: Ronnie O'Sullivan loses to Jiang Jun in Shenzhen Open second round
articles.summary: Seven-time world champion Ronnie O'Sullivan, world number one Zhao Xintong and defending champion Mark Williams lose on the opening day of the Shenzhen Open.
articles.body:
Seven-time world champion Ronnie O'Sullivan, world number one Zhao Xintong and defending champion Mark Williams were knocked out on the opening day of the Shenzhen Open.

China's Jiang Jun, who is 64th in the world rankings, took the opening two frames before England's O'Sullivan levelled with breaks of 92 and 52.

Jiang reeled off the next three frames, sealing a famous 5-2 second-round win with a superb break of 108 to set up a meeting with Englishman Zak Surety.

Scott Donaldson stunned 2025 world champion Zhao by winning a final-frame decider.

Scotland's Donaldson, who is 65 places below Zhao in the rankings, compiled breaks of 77, 105, 50 and 62 as he came from 3-2 down.

Donaldson will take on China's Pang Junxu in round three.

Welshman Williams lost 5-4 to China's Fan Zhengyi after fouling on the final pink.

England's Judd Trump cruised to a 5-0 win over China's Huang Jiahao and goes into the last 16 after Anthony McGill, his scheduled third-round opponent, withdrew on medical grounds.

In Monday's other second-round encounters, Australia's Neil Robertson beat China's Liu Hongyu 5-2, England's Chris Wakelin claimed a 5-3 win over Welshman Liam Davies and China's Si Jiahui swept to a 5-1 success against England's Oliver Lines.

Belgium's Ben Mertens also progressed as Northern Ireland's Mark Allen withdrew for personal reasons.

Wales' Jamie Clarke, England's Andrew Higginson, Hong Kong's Marco Fu and England's Sam Craigie progressed in the first-round matches that took place on Monday.

articles.body: NHL club Boston Bruins have reportedly rejected the trade offer for Detroit Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin amid their top-line center search. According to recent reports, the Bruins were among the teams that submitted an offer for Larkin.In fact, the Minnesota Wild also reportedly made an offer, with both proposals failing to result in a trade. The report did not specify whether Detroit rejected the offers or whether Larkin did, or who has trade protection, or whether that was involved in turning them down.It is important to note that the Detroit Red Wings have remained on the playoff bubble but have repeatedly fallen short with their performance, ending their postseason drought. In this season, they finished 41-31-10 in the Eastern Conference. Reports are indicating that the club's inability to return to the postseason and its direction under Steve Yzerman contributed to Larkin’s decision for a fresh start.Boston Bruins have Dylan Larkin trade offer rejected as the club continues its search for a centerAs Dylan Larkin has been one of the most influential faces of the Red Wings for several seasons, the Boston Bruins have reportedly made an offer for Detroit Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin, but the proposal was rejected. It has been clear that whether Detroit rejected the offers or Larkin.But, as per earlier reports, speculations suggest that the Michigan native has reportedly decided to move out of the Detroit Red Wings due to their inability to return to the postseason. This has fueled league-wide speculation regarding the captain's long-term future with the team.Dylan Larkin wants to leave the Detroit Red Wings, but he apparently does not want to go to the Boston Bruins. He gave Detroit a list of three teams that he would be willing to join and those were Florida Panthers, Minnesota Wild, and Vegas Golden Knights. Later, NHL insider Elliotte Friedman reported that Larkin had expanded his preferred list to around eight teams. But, Bruins are not on that list.Despite the significant hurdle in a trade for Larkin, the Boston Bruins are clearly trying their best to be contenders in the competitive Atlantic Division. The center position is particularly a potential weak spot for the club but for now the Boston club has Elias Lindholm, Pavel Zacha, Fraser Minten, and Sean Kuraly in their key role. Pierre LeBrun of The Athletic reported additional details:

This comes as Columbus and Marchenko have been unable to come to terms on a contract extension. He was also rather noncommittal about his status with the franchise when asked about his future in Columbus earlier this offseason:

Marchenko is scheduled for restricted free agency after the upcoming season, so there could be some motivation on Columbus' part to trade him if he has no interest in returning on an extension.

It would at least get something in return before he signs elsewhere down the line.

And there doesn't seem to be a shortage of suitors, as Friedman recently reported on his 32 Thoughts podcast (h/t Nick Goss of NBC Sports Boston).

"Montreal, everybody knows about, the Islanders I mentioned a couple pods ago," Friedman said. "Toronto I think has really tried to keep their interest secret, but it's kind of seeped out. I think Winnipeg at one point kind of looked into it.

"I heard Boston made an offer at one point. I had some people say Vegas, I had some other people say they weren't sure it was Vegas. I have to think Seattle is around this. They've really been looking at trying to grab a top-end player and they could make this deal."

So much interest from Toronto and others isn't particularly surprising, as Marchenko is 26 years old and coming off back-to-back impressive seasons. He scored 74 points on 43 assists and 31 goals in 2024-25 and then followed up with 67 points on 40 assists and 27 goals in 2025-26.

Given his age and the reality he was playing for a Blue Jackets team that missed the playoffs both seasons, it is reasonable to expect him to be even more productive in the future if he is surrounded by more talent on playoff contenders.

Toronto is certainly looking to return to the postseason after missing out last year.

It snapped a streak of nine straight seasons making the playoffs in part because of a middling offense that was 16th in the league in goals per game. Adding someone like Marchenko could help improve those numbers and perhaps lead to a return to the postseason.

articles.title: ¿Cobrará $25 millones por transmitir su parto? Karina García rompió el silencio tras la ola de críticas

articles.body: La creadora de contenido y modelo paisa Karina García volvió a quedar en el centro de la polémica digital tras los crecientes rumores que aseguraban que planeaba realizar una transmisión privada del nacimiento de su bebé a través de cobros a sus seguidores. En los últimos días, diversos usuarios y páginas de entretenimiento comenzaron a difundir que la empresaria estaría contemplando monetizar en vivo el momento de dar a luz, fijando presuntas tarifas que iban desde suscripciones privadas hasta cifras desorbitadas de 25 millones de pesos por acceso exclusivo. El rumor generó una ola de reacciones divididas en redes sociales. Mientras algunos usuarios criticaron la posibilidad de comercializar un evento tan íntimo, calificándolo de "espectáculo innecesario", otros lo tomaron con ironía y humor, cuestionando los límites del contenido en las plataformas digitales. Ante el revuelo mediático y los comentarios negativos que comenzaron a inundar sus perfiles, la influencer rompió el silencio para aclarar su posición. Karina desmintió las versiones que afirmaban que convertiría el nacimiento de su hijo en un evento de pago por evento. A través de sus historias y pronunciamientos con sus seguidores, la modelo aclaró el alcance de sus declaraciones previas sobre el proceso de gestación y cómo compartirá la llegada de su bebé con su audiencia. García enfatizó que, si bien acostumbra a hacer partícipes a sus fans de su vida cotidiana, el momento del parto es un evento de salud y privacidad que afrontará con los cuidados médicos requeridos, lejos de subastas o cobros a su comunidad.

articles.title: La FCF rompe el silencio tras graves acusaciones contra Ramón Jesurún por manejo arbitral
articles.standfirst: La tajante postura de la FCF ante los señalamientos contra Ramón Jesurún en la Liga BetPlay
articles.summary: La tajante postura de la FCF ante los señalamientos contra Ramón Jesurún en la Liga BetPlay
articles.body: La Federación Colombiana de Fútbol emitió un comunicado oficial en el que rechaza de manera categórica las acusaciones referentes a presuntas presiones e intervenciones directas de su presidente, Ramón Jesurún, en el nombramiento de los jueces encargados de impartir justicia en la Liga BetPlay. El pronunciamiento del máximo ente del balompié nacional surge tras la difusión de versiones periodísticas —provenientes de un medio de Manizales— que señalaban supuestas influencias o alteraciones dirigidas por la presidencia de la entidad en el arbitraje de la jornada 10 del torneo local. Frente a esto, la FCF sostuvo: “La FCF rechaza de manera categórica los señalamientos según los cuales su presidente, Ramón Jesurún, o terceros ajenos a la Comisión Arbitral Nacional habrían intervenido, directa o indirectamente, en la designación, modificación o sustitución de árbitros para partidos del fútbol colombiano”. Asimismo, la institución enfatizó la autonomía de la Comisión Arbitral Nacional, aclarando que ni la dirigencia principal ni personas externas poseen facultades legales ni reglamentarias para intervenir en dichas decisiones: En el mismo pronunciamiento, la FCF abordó el caso particular del colegiado Nicolás Gallo, a quien le fue extendida una invitación por parte del juez salvadoreño Iván Barton para desempeñarse en las funciones de VAR durante un partido de la Saudi Pro League en Arabia Saudita. La Federación aclaró la razón por la que no se le otorgó el permiso correspondiente: La negativa respondió estrictamente a la necesidad de cumplir con el calendario local y la programación de las competiciones del fútbol profesional colombiano. Con esta declaración, la FCF ratificó su compromiso con la institucionalidad, la transparencia y el estricto cumplimiento de la normativa que rige el balompié en el país.

articles.title: Miguel Borja iguala la marca de Hugo Sánchez en América
articles.standfirst: Miguel Borja al nivel de Hugo Sánchez: el récord histórico que logró en Club América
articles.summary: Miguel Borja al nivel de Hugo Sánchez: el récord histórico que logró en Club América
articles.body: El impacto de Miguel Ángel Borja en el fútbol mexicano ha sido inmediato y contundente. El delantero colombiano ha tenido un inicio con el Club América que no solo ilusiona a la afición azulcrema, sino que lo ha llevado a entrar directamente a los libros de historia de la institución al igualar una marca histórica que compartía hasta ahora un grupo muy reducido de leyendas, encabezado por el icónico delantero mexicano Hugo Sánchez. Desde su llegada al nido de Coapa, 'El Colibrí' ha necesitado muy pocos minutos para demostrar su poderío dentro del área. Con su reciente anotación en la victoria 2-4 frente a Necaxa por la Jornada 10 de la Liga MX, Borja llegó a la cifra de 4 goles en sus primeros 3 partidos oficiales disputados con la camiseta del América. Esta arranque lo sitúa a la par del registro que ostenta Hugo Sánchez desde agosto de 1992, cuando en sus primeros tres compromisos vestidos de azulcrema anotó cuatro tantos (ante Dallas Rockets y San Francisco Bay Blackhawks en la Concacaf). Solamente ocho futbolistas en la centenaria historia de las Águilas han alcanzado este registro al debutar, una lista selecta en la que el último caso se remontaba a más de dos décadas atrás (logrado por el peruano Luis Alberto 'El Chino' Ximénez en 2002). El gran momento del artillero colombiano no solo destaca por la cantidad de goles, sino también por la factura de los mismos. En el Clásico Nacional frente a Chivas de Guadalajara, Borja firmó una espectacular chilena que le dio la vuelta al continente. La acrobacia llamó de inmediato la atención del propio Hugo Sánchez, máximo referente mundial de los remates de chilena. A través de sus espacios en medios y redes sociales, 'El Pentapichichi' elogió públicamente la técnica del colombiano: "Quiero felicitar a Miguel Borja por la maravillosa chilena que firmó ante Chivas. Tremenda ejecución. Que vengan más golazos de este nivel. Para mí, el mejor gol hasta el momento del América en el Clásico Nacional", expresó la leyenda mexicana. El atacante cordobés ha mostrado una efectividad pasmosa con el esquema azulcrema: Miguel Ángel Borja ha caído de pie en la Liga MX, respondiendo con goles y jerarquía internacional para consolidarse como el referente de área que el América necesitaba para pelear lo más alto del torneo.

articles.title: Red Sox news: Payton Tolle gets Game 1 start in Wild Card Series vs. Yankees
articles.summary: The Boston Red Sox and New York Yankees will face off in the AL Wild Card Series this week. It is a rematch of the 2025 AL Wild Card Series that the Yankees...
articles.body:
The Boston Red Sox and New York Yankees will face off in the AL Wild Card Series this week. It is a rematch of the 2025 AL Wild Card Series that the Yankees won two games to one. Cam Schlittler won Game 3 of the series for the Yankees, and he will be on the mound for Game 1 in 2026.

Now, the Red Sox have announced who will be facing off against Schlittler, per Sean McAdam of MassLive.com.

" Payton Tolle is Game 1 starter for Red Sox," McAdam posted on X, formerly Twitter.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Tolle went 9-6 this past season with a 3.03 ERA and a 1.10 WHIP. It was his first full season in the majors for the left-handed pitcher. The 23-year-old also appeared in seven games in 2025, making three starts. Tolle did appear in the series against the Yankees last year. He came into Game 2 against the Yankees in the bottom of the eighth inning. The bases were loaded, and the Red Sox had just given up the lead. Tolle was able to get Trent Grisham to ground out on seven pitches, keeping it a one-run game. The Sox did not score in the top of the ninth, losing the game 4-3 and evening the best-of-three series.

Tolle faced the Yankees twice this year. He gave up just one run in six innings of work against the Yankees in April, but the Red Sox lost the game 4-2. He also faced them at the end of June, going seven innings without giving up a run as the Red Sox won the game 6-1.
