articles.title: Commanders QB Jayden Daniels traveling to London, possibly playing Colts
articles.summary: Jayden Daniels will return to Commanders practice this week in London, though playing prospects vs. Colts are uncertain
articles.body:
Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels will travel with the team to London in advance of a Week 4 clash with the Indianapolis Colts at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

While it's uncertain, and seemingly unlikely that Daniels will play in that game, the door's open just the slightest crack.

We know for sure that Daniels will start practicing with the team this week, a not too long after suffering a dislocated left elbow during a Week 2 loss at Dallas .

That starts Daniels' return to play process, an important step in getting him back on the field in games.

"He has been putting in the work," head coach Dan Quinn told reporters in a Monday virtual press conference . "I am excited to get him back on the practice field."

Daniels is not the only injured Commanders player going to London to start practice. Linebacker Frankie Luvu (groin) and tight end Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) will do the same, though the jury's still out on guard Sam Cosmi (concussion) and safety Nick Cross (internal/illness).

The Commanders leave for England on Tuesday evening.

Daniels' situation is a positive one that should include a return to play faster than he did in 2025, when he missed three games after suffering the same injury. Quinn didn't identify why there are different timelines, only that the team doing what it's told by doctors.

"We're just following the guidelines for him going through the process of him getting opinions from New York and L.A. sets the plan in motion," Quinn said. "We'll stick to that."

The Commanders will see how Daniels responds in practice and adjust its plans accordingly. Wednesday's session, after a long travel day, is more of a walk-through. Thursday will be more at full speed and provide a good indication of Daniels' status.

The same can be said for Luvu and Okonkwo.

"Once we get there, that'll give us a little more of an indication of where we're at and how we can go into that space," Quinn said. "Just the fact that we're working back into that space gives me optimism heading into the week about where we're at from a health perspective."

articles.title: LeBron James Alludes to Family Sacrifice as He Chases First Championship with 76ers
articles.summary: In a press conference on Monday, the NBA star sported his new jersey and shared some of the reasons that led him to sign with Philadelphia
articles.body:
LeBron James is speaking out about why he decided to sign with the 76ers

In his introductory press conference on Monday, the NBA star shared that his good friend Tyrese Maxey played a role

James also shared that he wanted to join a team that had a viable chance to win a championship

LeBron James may be wearing a new jersey but the loyalty he has to his family has never wavered.

In his first press conference with the Philadelphia 76ers on Monday, Sept. 28 — and after months of buzz regarding his surprise decision — the NBA star, 41, laid out what led him to sign with the team.

James pointed to Sixers star guard Tyrese Maxey — his good friend — as one of the "main deciding factors" in joining the squad.

"I was asking all the questions that I could ask him," James shared about their multiple exchanges. "It wasn't just one conversation. Our relationship, when I broke a lot of the teams and franchises down I could possibly play for, he was one of the main deciding factors."

But as for family, James puts his wife Savannah and their kids, Bronny, Bryce and Zhuri first.

"You have to fall in love with doing things that's uncomfortable and if we can do that then we can be a great team," James said. "If we don't do that then we be like, 'Oh man, it was a great team on paper and we had a lot of great talent and we lost in the second round.' Like I don't want to do that."

He added, "I didn't leave my family to lose in the second round, I know that for sure."

Last year in his eighth season with the Los Angeles Lakers , the team lost in the second round to the Oklahoma City Thunder .

With his new team, James shared that he is willing to do "whatever the team needs" for him to do.

"It's going to take time. ... Everyone wants instant oatmeal. ... If you want something special, it takes time and every single day, doing something that you may not want to do," he said. "In order for us to be great, we have to do things that are just not comfortable. We have to be comfortable being uncomfortable. That is the best way to expedite being great."

The 76ers tip off the regular season on Tuesday, Oct. 20 against the defending champions, the New York Knicks .

articles.title: Sam Darnold Reveals How His Body Felt in Seahawks’ Shocking Loss to Commanders
articles.summary: Sam Darnold’s return to the Seattle Seahawks‘ starting lineup in Week 3 was anything but quiet. After missing two games with a glute injury suffered in the s...
articles.body:
Sam Darnold 's return to the Seattle Seahawks ' starting lineup in Week 3 was anything but quiet. After missing two games with a glute injury suffered in the season opener.

Darnold stepped back under center and posted a career-high passing performance, yet his return was ultimately spoiled by costly turnovers in a 33-31 road loss to the Washington Commanders . How he felt physically was a concern, but that is now out of the question as he opened up about it postgame.

Sam Darnold opens up on return that did not go as planned

Sam Darnold sustained a unique soft-tissue glute injury on the opening drive of the Seattle Seahawks ' Week 1 victory over the New England Patriots after being sacked by pass rusher Dre'Mont Jones. Immediately after the hit, Darnold experienced persistent pain that prevented him from throwing. Initial fears pointed toward a potential season-ending hip issue.

However, subsequent MRI scans ruled out a hip injury and identified a glute muscle issue instead, drastically shortening his expected recovery timeline from months to just a couple of weeks.

Darnold cleared injury protocol and made his return in Week 3 against the Washington Commanders after logging full practice sessions leading up to the game. Before kickoff, Darnold put his body through rigorous physical tests during pre-warmups and padded drills to ensure he could move, drop back, and extend plays safely.

Despite feeling physically "great", Sam Darnold was critical of his performance in the game they lost to Commanders with a close margin.

"Physically I feel great. I really tried to test it pregame. Pre-pre-warmup and then with the pads on," Darnold said on his performance. "Obviously, not the outcome that we wanted. Too many turnovers. We didn't execute enough in the red zone. We just got to be better. First downs we can be more efficient. I feel like as a whole, our offense can be more efficient and better operationally as well."

Regarding the decisive interception returned for a touchdown, Darnold admitted it was a poor decision, noting that he saw the defender coming and should have thrown the ball into the dirt. Nevertheless, they face Los Angeles Chargers in Week 4, who considerably have a weaker defense sanding with 0-3 so far.

Sam Darnold will face Chargers' defense in Week 4

The Los Angeles Chargers defense has endured a difficult start to the season, struggling across multiple areas. Entering Week 3, the Chargers ranked 26th in the NFL in passing yards allowed per game, routinely giving up chunk plays through the air and failing to consistently restrict opposing quarterbacks. In their 24-16 loss to the Buffalo Bills , Los Angeles allowed 176 rushing yards on the ground.

Despite throwing two costly interceptions, Darnold had a good game against the Seahawks. He completed 31 of 45 pass attempts for a career-high 379 passing yards and 4 touchdown passes, finishing with a 105.7 passer rating. Now, Darnold gets a prime opportunity to rebound against a Chargers defense that ranks near the bottom of the league in overall yardage allowed and efficiency.

Fresh off a career-high 379 passing yards and 4 touchdowns against the Commanders, Darnold is well-positioned to exploit Los Angeles ' porous pass defense if he minimizes bad decisions and protects the football.

articles.title: 3 reasons why Dodgers could fail in pursuit of World Series three-peat
articles.summary: These are three big problems for the Dodgers this October.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are entering the MLB postseason with a first-round bye, but they are not the No. 1 seed. That goes to the Milwaukee Brewers . But this Dodgers team should still be considered the World Series favorites with their stacked roster.

In pursuit of a third-straight World Series title, this Dodgers team is going to have a real chance to win it all this Fall. But that doesn't mean things cannot go wrong.

ESPN's Jorge Castillo revealed three reasons why the Dodgers could get eliminated early this postseason, and all three are real issues that have been impacting the Dodgers this season.

3 reasons why Dodgers could fail in three-peat quest

"If they go home early, it will be because age, injuries and their back-to-back World Series runs caught up with them," Castillo writes.

Injuries, age, and fatigue are the three reasons why the Dodgers could fail in their pursuit of a third-straight World Series championship.

Regarding age, the Dodgers have the oldest roster in the Major Leagues, coming in at 31.1 years old, according to Castillo. Freddie Freeman , Mookie Betts , Shohei Ohtani , and plenty of others are over 30 years old.

While age might not be the sole reason for their failure this October, it could play a real role, especially when combined with another big reason why 2026 could be a failure: fatigue.

The Dodgers have played more games than any other team in MLB over the last three seasons, as they've gone on deep runs every year so far. It would not be a surprise if the Dodgers simply ran out of steam.

That is sort of what happened to the Kansas City Chiefs in their three-peat pursuit. They were demolished in the Super Bowl, their third-straight title appearance, by the Philadelphia Eagles. The next season was a huge regression year as well.

While not solely due to fatigue, it certainly played a role. That could end up being a reason why the Dodgers struggle in October this year, as the Chiefs did in 2025.

But the other major issue, and easily the most pressing, is the injuries. Ohtani is hurt enough to keep him off the mound, while players like Andy Pages , Will Smith , Brock Stewart , Blake Treinen , Roki Sasaki , and Justin Wrobleski are all coming off injuries.

While the Dodgers might've gotten these injured players back, there will be some real questions about how they play in October.

Between injuries, the Dodgers' roster's age, and the fatigue of multiple title runs, the Dodgers could end up failing in their World Series pursuit. This team has a real chance of winning it all, but these underrated issues could sink their season.

articles.title: Mets expect to be 'looking externally' for first base help this offseason
articles.summary: Mets president of baseball operations expects the Mets to look both internally and externally to fill first base in 2027.
articles.body:
If Bo Bichette opts in for the 2027 season, the Mets will likely be set when it comes to most of their starting lineup, perhaps leaving first base and designated hitter as the two easiest ways for them to reshape the offense this offseason.

With that as a backdrop, president of baseball operations David Stearns spoke on Monday about the team's struggle to fill first base in 2026 after Pete Alonso signed a five-year deal with the Baltimore Orioles last offseason. On the decision to let Alonso walk, Stearns said he doesn't get "mulligans."

As far as how the Mets will address first base this offseason?

"I do think it's potentially a combination of internal pieces and external," Stearns explained. "I don't think, sitting up here right now, I'm gonna close the door on anything. I think Jared Young had a really good second half of the season. When we gave him consistent playing time, he responded and performed.

"I think what we saw from Brett Baty , particularly over the last four-to-six weeks where he was one of the best offensive players in all of baseball -- we need to see him do that more consistently. Brett knows that. But I don't want to undercount that as well. We have other internal options, and I also think we're going to be looking externally as well."

On Baty specifically, Stearns was forthright regarding the possibility that his strong finish was fool's gold.

In parts of five big league seasons with the Mets, Baty has showed promise at the plate, including when he posted a .748 OPS in 2025. But he has not been consistent enough.

"The truth is, we won't know," Stearns said about whether Baty can carry over his end-of-season success to 2027. "I do think having been around Brett for multiple years now, I think where he is from a mindset perspective, his level of belief in himself, and how he works through an at-bat, is different right now. But as with any player, until you see it for an extended period, very difficult for me to sit here right now and have complete certainty on that."

Regarding other internal options at first base, Jorge Polanco is theoretically one of them.

But Polanco missed the majority of this season due to a lingering ankle injury that required season-ending surgery. When he was on the field, he struggled badly, putting up a 22 OPS+ in 37 games.

And Stearns doesn't have illusions about what to expect from Polanco in 2027, which is the second and final year of the contract he inked last offseason.

"With Jorge, the early stages of the rehab are going really well," Stearns said. "I know, having gotten to know the person over the last year, he's going to work exceptionally hard to put himself in position to contribute. I also don't know the exact extent of what that's going to look like. I'm not gonna sit here and say he's gonna play 120 games at first base.

"I think we need to wait and see where he is in spring training. I know that when he's healthy, this is a really good offensive player from both sides of the plate who can hit in the middle of the lineup and do a bunch of different things. I would love to have that version of player on the team, and I'm looking forward to seeing what we get in spring training."

When it comes to external options, the free agent market isn't particularly enticing.

Ty France is coming off a huge season for the Padres (career-best .865 OPS), but is entering his age-32 season and is one year removed from signing a minor league deal.

An intriguing option could be Japanese slugger Teruaki Sato , who is expected to be posted for big league clubs this offseason.

Sato, 27, has been primarily a third baseman and outfielder in Japan, but could slide across the diamond to first base in the majors.

Sato smacked 37 homers in 136 games this season for the Hanshin Tigers while posting a career-best OPS of 1.017.

articles.title: Dobnak’s Blunder Can’t Erase White Sox Playoff Run
articles.summary: Randy Dobnak's pickoff error gave the White Sox their first playoff berth since 2021. A messy end to the Royals season, but the future looks bright.
articles.body:
The party started early at Kauffman Stadium on Thursday, but the Kansas City Royals were the ones getting soaked. The Chicago White Sox rolled past the home team 9-1 to lock up their first playoff spot since 2021, and the cost was steep for the locals. Pitcher Randy Dobnak gave up six runs in just 1.1 innings, and his mistakes were the main reason the celebration happened on the visiting team's turf. This wasn't just a loss; it was a blown opportunity for a season that already felt like a long slog.

Everything fell apart in the first two innings when Dobnak couldn't hold the White Sox hitters. A throwing error on a bunt opened the door, and Miguel Vargas drove in the first run with an RBI single. Things got worse in the second inning when he tried to pick off a runner but threw to first base with nobody covering the bag. That blunder let Braden Montgomery score easily from second base. Dobnak admitted the confusion after the game, telling reporters, "As far as I'm aware, I don't know if I've even practiced that with the Royals yet. But that's on me, I got to know what to do." It is a rare moment of honesty from a player who just handed a division rival a ticket to the postseason.

While the scoreline looked ugly, the mood in the stadium was weirdly friendly because of the connections between the two clubs. White Sox general manager Chris Getz played for the Royals and worked in their front office before taking his current job. He thanked the Kansas City staff for making the trip special, saying, "They've gone out of their way to make sure that this was a special experience for us. But I'm just happy for this group. Happy, happy for the Chicago White Sox and our fan base." Former Royals executive Jin Wong also joined the White Sox staff, and he noted that Getz called him out of the blue to join the team. These personal bonds made the loss feel like a betrayal to some, but the White Sox fans just wanted to win.

Maikel Garcia , who had a great game the night before, said the team just wants to end on a high note. "It's not fun playing when you're not in the playoffs," Garcia said after the game, per reports. "So we're just trying to play to finish this season strong as a team and focus on next year." The focus now shifts to spring training and hoping Dobnak can prove Thursday was just a bad day.

articles.title: Best and worst offensive PFF grades for Patriots in loss to Jaguars
articles.summary: Here are the best and worst-graded Patriots players from Sunday's Week 3 loss to the Jaguars.
articles.body:
The New England Patriots lost to the Jacksonville Jaguars 35-6 in Week 3 and did not turn in their best offensive performance by any means, to put it lightly.

Patriots quarterback Drake Maye completed 14-of-25 passes for 199 yards, no touchdowns and threw two interceptions in the game. New England 's running game was quiet, as TreVeyon Henderson went for 23 rushing yards and Rhamondre Stevenson registered 22 yards. Mack Hollins was the team's best performer on the day with a team-high six catches for 87 yards.

Romeo Doubs cooled off from his emergent game in Week 2, going for 49 receiving yards against the Jaguars. articles.title: Dolphins Get Major RB Update After De’Von Achane Injury News
articles.summary: The Miami Dolphins left their 24-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs with a 0-3 record. De’Von Achane exited early with a knee injury, forcing Miami to adjust...
articles.body:
The Miami Dolphins left their 24-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs with a 0-3 record. De'Von Achane exited early with a knee injury, forcing Miami to adjust its backfield in a difficult home opener.

Achane had three carries for 17 yards before leaving the game. Ollie Gordon II took over and handled most of the work, while Jaylen Wright was inactive because of a stinger and foot injury. Malik Washington also became an emergency option at running back.

The Dolphins now face an important adjustment ahead of their Week 4 trip to Minnesota to face the Vikings.

Head coach Jeff Hafley acknowledged the uncertainty immediately after Sunday's game, saying, "To be very honest with you, it does not sound very optimistic at this moment, but I can't give you any other details until I have them."

Dolphins Turn to Jaylen Wright & Ollie Gordon After De'Von Achane Injury

Sun Sentinel's David Furones reported that , "The Dolphins will move forward with Jaylen Wright and Ollie Gordon at RB on the roster."

Furones also noted that Wright was sidelined Sunday because of his stinger and foot issue, leaving Gordon to handle the workload after Achane went down.

Gordon carried the ball 18 times after Achane's departure, according to Furones' report, while wide receiver Malik Washington served as Miami's emergency third running back.

Miami can also elevate Jarquez Hunter or Carlos Washington from the practice squad or explore an outside signing.

The update follows confirmation that Achane suffered a torn ACL and will miss the remainder of the season.

The injury occurred on his third rushing attempt against Kansas City when his left leg gave out as he planted to make a cut.

Gordon finished the game with 17 official carries for 41 yards and a touchdown.

He also caught three passes for 14 yards. His touchdown came on a 3-yard run during Miami's 91-yard opening scoring drive.

Gordon briefly left the game with cramps but returned and continued handling the majority of Miami's rushing work.

Wright's health will now be an important factor in determining the backfield rotation.

The former Tennessee running back has three carries this season and missed Sunday's game after dealing with a stinger and foot injury.

Miami also has Hunter and Carlos Washington available on its practice squad. The Dolphins could bring either player onto the active roster if additional depth is needed.

Dolphins Rookie Chris Bell Emerges Against Chiefs

Miami also received an encouraging performance from rookie wide receiver Chris Bell during Sunday's loss.

Bell caught four of seven targets for 67 yards, including a 44-yard reception.

It was a significant improvement from his first two games, when he had only one catch for 25 yards.

Bell received more opportunities with rookie receiver Caleb Douglas sidelined by an ankle injury.

His performance gave quarterback Malik Willis another young option in the passing game.

Willis completed 20 of 36 passes for 210 yards against Kansas City and added 56 rushing yards.

The Dolphins also continued to rely on their running game despite losing Achane early.

Miami will now travel to Minnesota for Week 4. With Achane unavailable, Gordon and Wright are expected to form the core of the backfield, provided Wright is healthy enough to return.

The Dolphins can also turn to their practice squad or the outside market for additional depth as they adjust to Achane's season-ending injury.

articles.title: Angels’ Mike Trout wants to make big change after 100-loss season
articles.summary: Los Angeles Angels star Mike Trout wants to make a major change for one reason.
articles.body:
Mike Trout has spent most of his career patrolling center field for the Los Angeles Angels . After a 100-loss season , the three-time AL MVP is willing to give it up if it helps the team move forward.

That is a notable change for Trout, who entered 2026 determined to return to center field after spending much of the previous season as a designated hitter. He had said he felt more comfortable there and believed the position suited his body better.

The Angels finished 62-100 after Sunday's loss to the Seattle Mariners , officially recording the first 100-loss season in franchise history. After a year like that, even one of baseball's biggest stars appears ready to rethink where he fits.

Trout has offered to move to left field and take on more work as a designated hitter, according to Rhett Bollinger of MLB.com.

That is not exactly the kind of offseason adjustment most players volunteer for. But Trout has a pretty good reason.

Mike Trout is willing to move for the Angels

The Angels need to improve after allowing 752 runs and finishing at the bottom of the AL West. Trout's willingness to move around could give the club more flexibility as John Mozeliak reshapes the roster.

It also comes after another season in which injuries remained part of the conversation around Trout. He dealt with a right hamstring strain during the season, adding to the long list of physical setbacks that have limited his availability in recent years.

Still, Trout managed to appear in 139 games and finish with a .242 batting average, 22 home runs and 54 RBI, according to the supplied 2026 statistics.

Los Angeles Angels right fielder Mike Trout (27) comes to bat in the first inning of the MLB Interleague game between the Cincinnati Reds and the Los Angeles Angels at Great American Ball Park in downtown Cincinnati on Friday, April 10, 2026.

The interesting part is that Trout is not simply asking the Angels to build around him in the same way they always have. He is offering to change his role.

That could mean more time at DH, more games in left field and less responsibility in center.

For a player who once preferred center field so strongly that he specifically asked to return there, that is a meaningful shift.

The Angels have plenty of work ahead after going 62-100. At least their biggest star is already showing a willingness to move a few pieces around.

articles.title: Nick Saban reveals Alabama secretly recorded him, teases Tua Tagovailoa conversation in new doc
articles.summary: "Saban" is a six-part documentary coming out in October.
articles.body:
Nick Saban revealed Alabama has archived footage of team meetings that he didn't know about.

Now, that video, including when he told quarterback Tua Tagovailoa he was replacing Jalen Hurts at quarterback, will be featured in "Saban," a six-part documentary on the former Alabama coach .

"When I told Tua that he was going in at halftime for Jalen, I didn't know any of that (footage) existed," Saban told Rich Eisen about the 2017-18 national championship game in which Tagovailoa led Alabama past Georgia in overtime with the infamous second and 26 play. "So to see all of that inside out sort of stuff that happens behind the scenes, I thought would be very, very interesting for fans in terms of the competitive nature of sports."

Saban said 70 people were interviewed for the documentary, which he says goes behind the scenes.

He said Alabama never told him they were recording behind the scenes in the locker room and in tea meetings.

"I would never let the media in the locker room after the game," Saban said. "I thought there was a time when they coach-team relationship was very important.

"What you said to the team was not for public information. Well, Alabama was doing an archive on all those things. I never knew that stuff existed."

"Saban" will premiere on Oct. 8, at 5 p.m. Central (6 p.m. ET/3 p.m. PT). Subsequent episodes will air throughout October and into November on ESPN.

The documentary series traces Saban's early life in West Virginia and at Kent State University and his coaching career from low-level assistant to young head coach on through the glory years at Alabama, where he won six national championships in 17 seasons before retiring in early 2024. Saban and wife Terry are interviewed extensively in the series, along with more than 70 friends, coaching colleagues and former players such as Bill Belichick, Lane Kiffin, Steve Sarkisian, Kirby Smart, Jalen Hurts, Derrick Henry , Bryce Young , Julio Jones , AJ McCarron , DeVonta Smith and Tua Tagovailoa.

"With my coaching days behind me, Miss Terry and I have been doing a lot of reflection and realized we were ready to tell our story," Saban said last month . "The team at Words + Pictures has encouraged me to really look back not just at my time at Alabama, but every stop along the way – and not just reflect on what happened but consider the process which made it happen. I interacted with a lot of players and coaches along the way and I'm happy to see that so many of them have contributed to this docuseries. There's a lot to tell, and I'm excited to share it all."

"Saban" also promises never-before-aired footage from practices, sidelines, locker rooms and other "behind-the-scenes" moments.

"Nick Saban's impact extends far beyond the championships and historic success he achieved on the field," said Brian Lockhart, Senior Vice President, ESPN Original Content. "What makes this series so special is the extraordinary access to Coach Saban, Miss Terry and the people who know him best, paired with rare footage that offers a new perspective on his remarkable journey. Saban is a definitive portrait of one of the most consequential figures in college football history, and we're proud to share it with fans."

articles.title: 2 players most to blame for Mariners' miserable season
articles.summary: The Seattle Mariners entered 2026 with championship expectations after an ALCS appearance, only to be eliminated from postseason contention before the final...
articles.body:
The Seattle Mariners entered 2026 with championship expectations after an ALCS appearance, only to be eliminated from postseason contention before the final weekend. Injuries, shaky pitching and defensive lapses created a team-wide failure, but the lineup's biggest problem was that its two franchise faces failed to produce at anything close to their normal standard.

Cal Raleigh and Julio Rodriguez are not solely responsible for Seattle's collapse. They are, however, the two players whose regression most clearly transformed a club built to contend into one watching October baseball from home.

Cal Raleigh 's regression buried the middle of the lineup

Raleigh's 2025 breakout established him as one of the game's premier catchers and a legitimate MVP-caliber force. Seattle needed even a modest version of that player in 2026. Instead, it received one of the sport's most jarring year-over-year offensive crashes.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Raleigh closed the season with a .182 average and .664 OPS, though he did reach 23 homers and 69 RBIs in 126 games. Those totals may look passable in isolation, particularly for a catcher, but they barely resemble the impact Seattle expected from the player who had become its central power threat.

The slump was not brief, either. In May, Raleigh went 43 consecutive plate appearances without a hit and carried a .166/.249/.325 slash line. His OPS had fallen 384 points from the prior season at that stage, while his hard-hit rate plummeted from 50 percent to 29 percent.

Injury context matters as Raleigh dealt with right-side discomfort early, then suffered a right oblique injury against Kansas City on May 1. The Mariners initially let him attempt to play through the issue before placing him on the injured list, and Raleigh later conceded that grinding through it was not helping either himself or the club.

Still, Seattle built its order around Raleigh's ability to punish mistakes from both sides of the plate. When the cleanup-level bat produced a .567 OPS through Aug. 20 and struggled against fastballs he had crushed a year earlier, opponents could attack the Mariners' lineup far more aggressively. A late September rebound could not repair the months of missing production.

Julio Rodriguez never became Seattle's engine

Rodriguez's season was less catastrophic than Raleigh's, but his failure carries a different kind of weight. Superstars are supposed to lift a team through its rough stretches. Seattle needed Rodríguez to establish the offensive floor every day, especially once Raleigh's slump became undeniable. Instead, its $200 million centerpiece delivered career lows in batting average, slugging percentage, OPS and WAR.

Rodriguez finished with a .247 average, 22 home runs, 71 RBIs, 22 steals and a .708 OPS in 150 games. The 20-homer, 20-steal benchmark is impressive, but it cannot conceal the decline. His .708 OPS was well below his .783 career mark entering the season, and his .401 slugging percentage showed how rarely he supplied the game-changing impact expected from an elite center fielder.

The story gets more complicated because Rodriguez suffered a concussion on July 3 , and his numbers sagged thereafter. He posted a .259 average, .424 slugging percentage and 117 wRC+ before the injury; afterward, those marks fell to .239, .383 and 93, respectively. His defensive work also slipped, an uncharacteristic issue for one of baseball's premier athletes.

But injuries explain only so much. Rodriguez had shown signs of a real step forward in May, when he hit 10 homers and slugged .590. He never sustained it, leaving Seattle without the consistent star production that turns a talented roster into a dangerous one.

Raleigh's collapse created a massive hole in the heart of the order; Rodriguez's down year denied the Mariners the superstar ceiling needed to compensate. Seattle's miserable season had plenty of contributors, from poor pitching to roster flaws, but these two fell shortest relative to their roles—and the Mariners paid for it every day.

articles.title: LeBron James' 1-Word Assessment of Ex-Celtics Star Jaylen Brown Says It All

articles.body:
It sounds like Jaylen Brown is entering the 2026-27 NBA season with something to prove.

During media day, LeBron James was asked about his thoughts on some of his new Philadelphia 76ers teammates.

When it came to Brown, James had one word to describe the former Boston Celtics star.

James' answer is particularly notable given everything Brown has gone through over the last 12 months.

Brown is coming off the best season of his career. He averaged career highs of 28.7 points, 6.9 rebounds and 5.1 assists per game while serving as the No. 1 option on a Celtics team that won 56 games. He earned his fifth All-Star selection and second All-NBA selection while finishing sixth in MVP voting.

Despite those numbers, the Celtics traded Brown to the 76ers for Paul George , two first-round picks and two second-round picks. Brown has also had to deal with criticism, from being called the seventh-best player on a team by an "analytics guy" to a " disease " by two people in the league.

James and Brown haven't even spent much time together, but James already sees Brown is motivated.

articles.title: Scranton/Wilkes-Barre RailRiders’ season filled with highlights, memorable moments
articles.summary: From callups, debuts and rehab assignments to milestones and records, Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre witnessed a lot
articles.body:
Although they missed the playoffs, the season was a successful one for the Scranton/Wilkes-Barre RailRiders. They finished 78-68 overall — 41-31 in the second half — and were in contention for the postseason until the final weekend.

This was the final season that Scranton/Wilkes-Barre will be known as the RailRiders; the team is rebranding next season.

"As a team, we were able to do a lot of good things and play some really good baseball for the most part," pitcher Brendan Beck said. "It's a bummer we came up a little short in the playoff push, but only one team can make it. We were playing meaningful baseball until the very end, so it was a good year."

Beck, the Yankees' No. 27 prospect according to MLB Pipeline , provided perhaps the biggest highlight of the season on June 5 at Syracuse when he combined with Carson Coleman on a no-hitter — the seventh in franchise history (third nine-inning). The right-hander was named International League Pitcher of the Year after finishing tied for second in wins with 10 and leading the league in ERA (2.93), strikeouts (151), innings (135.1), WHIP (1.06), and opponents' batting average (.210). His strikeout total ranks fourth in franchise single-season history and his ERA ranks fifth.

On May 7, Beck made his major-league debut at Yankee Stadium against the Texas Rangers. Other RailRiders who got the call and made their major league debuts included Elmer Rodriguez (April 29), George Lombard Jr. (Aug. 4), Bradley Hanner (Aug. 14) and Alexander Cornielle (Sept. 25).

Rodriguez joined Beck on the International League All-Star team. The right-hander, who is the Yankees' No. 2 prospect, went 8-4 with the RailRiders with a 2.45 ERA and 105 strikeouts in 106.1 innings.

Not only did the RailRiders have players who went up, but they also had a number of players come down, such as Jasson Dominguez , Anthony Volpe , and J.C. Escarra . Several Yankees players also did rehab assignments — pitchers Gerrit Cole , Max Fried , Carlos Rodon , catcher Austin Wells , and outfielder Cody Bellinger .

"There's been more movement on this team, more back and forth turnover with position players and pitchers than any team I've been on," manager Shelley Duncan said. "Had a lot of guys come down from the big leagues with a tough mindset and they really gave themselves to the team. A lot of guys here with deep, strong individual aspirations and they poured themselves into the team. I've seen us go through stretches where things were bleak and they don't give up hope or shut it down. They fight through it. I've seen players grow, I've seen some guys have some unbelievable years. I've seen some guys make some big career jumps. There's a lot this season."

Besides Beck, several other RailRiders ranked among the International League leaders. Yanquiel Fernandez tied for third in home runs with 27, ranked third in RBIs with 87, and tied for ninth in hits with 126. Oswaldo Cabrera tied for fifth in hits with 134 and was 10th in batting at .288 (134 for 466).

Duke Ellis finished second in the league in stolen bases with 60, one behind Worcester's Braiden Ward. Ellis set the franchise single-season record for steals, breaking the mark of 44 set by the Red Barons' Tommy Barrett in 1989. He also became the franchise's career leader in steals with 102, surpassing the record of 82 held by the Red Barons' Nick Punto . Ellis also ended the season with a 15-game hitting streak and a 20-game on-base streak.

Another highlight was a season-high eight-game winning streak from July 26 to Aug. 4, including a six-game series sweep in Iowa against the Chicago Cubs ' Triple-A affiliate. It was the first time since 1990 that a Scranton/Wilkes-Barre team visited Iowa.

That winning streak gave the RailRiders a 23-9 record in the second half, good for first place in the standings by one game over the Durham Bulls and two over the Indianapolis Indians. However, they lost their next four games to Rochester at PNC Field by a combined 40-11 and that was the turning point for the RailRiders. Interestingly, that also was the turning point for the Red Wings and as they went 27-14 the rest of the way to win the second-half title, then capture the league championship over the first-half champion Memphis Redbirds. Rochester lost to the Pacific Coast League champion Oklahoma City Comets in 10 innings, 5-3, in the Triple-A National Championship Game in Las Vegas.

"It's really a shame we were not in the playoffs," relief pitcher Eric Reyzelman said. "I feel if this team got a chance to play in there, we would have been the last team coming out of Vegas. It's tough the way it ended, but we played hard until the last second."

While winning a championship would have been a storybook ending to the RailRiders era, it was still an exciting, memorable season.

articles.title: After shutout loss, UAlbany football trying to correct red-zone frustrations
articles.summary: UAlbany has scored 12 times in 18 trips into the red zone, a league-worst 66.7% success rate that's tied for 102nd nationally in the Football Championship Su...
articles.body:
The University at Albany football team has come up empty in the red zone too often to satisfy head coach Tom Perkovich.

It's an area Perkovich, whose team has lost back-to-back games, plans to work on leading into Saturday's nonleague finale against Delaware State at Casey Stadium.

The Great Danes' offense ranks last in the Coastal Athletic Association in efficiency in the red zone, defined as the area between the opponent's 20-yard line and the end zone. UAlbany has scored 12 times in 18 trips into the red zone, a league-worst 66.7% success rate that's tied for 102nd nationally in the Football Championship Subdivision.

"We've got to -- obviously -- execute better in the red zone," Perkovich said Monday during the CAA coaches' media conference call. "That's hurt us big-time in the last few weeks."

UAlbany (2-3) failed to score inside the 5 in the final minutes of a 21-17 loss at Buffalo on Sept. 3 and in a 28-20 defeat against Monmouth on Sept. 19. The Great Danes were 0-for-2 in the red zone in Saturday's 22-0 loss at Princeton.

This past weekend, quarterback Kai Colon threw an ill-advised pass under pressure for an interception at the Princeton 3 in the second quarter. Later, the Great Danes had the ball at the Tigers 1 early in the fourth quarter, but backup quarterback Aidan Semo lost a yard on third down and a Colon pass to Tavahri Groves was broken up on fourth.

"We need to probably get a little bit more creative and do some different things," said Perkovich, who is the offensive play-caller. "I thought we had some things dialed up. It comes down to execution of our jobs and being able to pin your ears back, and go and get physical. We've got to figure it out."

Perkovich said he'd like to get the ball more to wide receiver BJ Norman and running back Rahshan La Mons in the red zone.

"Trying to get those guys involved more," Perkovich said. "We're struggling to get the passing game going and (to) get those guys on the perimeter the ball. We've got to do a better job of that."

He also emphasized protecting Colon and Semo better.

"That's really hurt us over the last few weeks," Perkovich said.

UAlbany began the Princeton game with Jackson Nixon, who has played center, moving outside to left tackle. William Van Neil, a transfer from Division III Anna Maria College, started at center. Later in the game, Nixon moved back inside to center with Shaker High graduate Emmitt Harris coming off the bench to play left tackle.

On a positive note, UAlbany has scored 12 touchdowns in the red zone, tied for fourth in the CAA. However, the Great Danes are the league's only team that hasn't kicked a red-zone field goal.

"We've got to be OK with playing for three (points) sometimes when it doesn't go our way," Perkovich said. "We can't force things. I think we're forcing things. We're tight because of what's happened. We've just got to play football and us, as coaches, probably have to do a better job of getting creative down there, and giving some different looks and different presentations, and try to find a way to get in the end zone."

Perkovich said he could see UAlbany doing "a little bit" more work than usual in the red zone in practice this week.

The Great Danes will try to get back on track against Delaware State (3-2) of the Mid-Eastern Athletic Conference, coached by former NFL wide receiver DeSean Jackson , before heading into their bye week. After that, UAlbany returns to CAA play for the rest of the season.

Delaware State beat UAlbany 37-32 last season.

Perkovich wants to see his team play "with some pride" in front of a homecoming crowd on Saturday.

"As I say to our staff, we're not throwing the baby out with the bath water," he said. "We're not throwing the whole thing out. We're still working on the things we know we can do, and maybe add some wrinkles and do that."

articles.title: The Seahawks special teams is not off to a great start in one key area
articles.summary: The Seahawks were one of the league’s best at covering kickoffs last season. That has not been the case in 2026.
articles.body:
When the Seattle Seahawks slogged their way through a pretty uninspired preseason, the special teams concern was the performance of Jason Myers , who missed five kicks over three games. Myers has been perfect on his field goals and extra points, which is a big relief.

But through three weeks of the regular season, the Seahawks have a different special teams issue that definitely was not a problem in 2025.

The Seahawks are one of the worst teams at defending kick returns

Last season, Jay Harbaugh's unit allowed only 24 yards per kick return, tied for fourth-fewest in the NFL and almost two full yards below the league average. Seattle allowed 81 returns (second-most in the league) while Jason Myers had a career-low 17.5% touchback rate, so the Seahawks having a high-scoring offense was only part of the equation. This was a team that was willing to put the ball in play and limit the opposition to much worse field position than a touchback at the 35.

According to Stathead , the average starting field position for Seahawks opponents off of kickoffs was their own 28, the worst in the NFL (well, best, if you look at it from Seattle's perspective).

With Week 3 almost wrapped up, the Seahawks rank 30th in yards per return allowed at 30.1 . They have already allowed five of 11 kickoffs to be run back for at least 30 yards. In 2025, the Seahawks only allowed eight such returns. The average starting field position for Seahawks opponents off of kickoffs is their own 32, which is worse than league average and includes touchbacks and illegal kicks that bring the ball to the 40.

I'm no film expert, but the Seahawks look to be having trouble with outside contain and getting off their blocks in the first place. In none of these returns is the returner contacted until they're just about at the 30.

I stress that this is only a kickoff return problem, because the Seahawks are the only team in the NFL yet to even allow a punt return.

If the Seahawks coverage unit cannot consistently make returns significantly better than a 35-yard line touchback, then Jason Myers might as well just kick more touchbacks when possible. Seattle has been really, close to letting a big return break and the dam might burst sooner rather than later.

Losing Dareke Young , Cody White , and Jake Bobo could be looming large

The Seahawks didn't lose too many players from last season's roster, but 15 of those kick return tackles last year came from current Las Vegas Raiders , Dareke Young and Cody White. Young was second behind Brady Russell in kick return tackles, while White had six before suffering a season-ending injury. Jake Bobo is still on the team but on injured reserve for the year. That's a combined 407 special teams snaps lost to injury or departures. Seattle usually had at least one of those three receivers on kick coverage duties, and during the playoffs (when White was on IR) the Seahawks had Bobo and Young together.

It's not nothing that Montorie Foster Jr, star of Hard Knocks and one of the preseason standouts over the summer, has been a healthy scratch for two games. Foster played seven special teams snaps (three punts, four kickoffs) and that's the extent of his action up to this point. Seattle has played two straight games without a receiver covering kicks.

After Week 4, Irv Charles is available to come off injured reserve. There is zero chance he's going to do anything on offense, not when he's pushing 30 and has zero career targets. But he was acquired in the offseason because , when healthy, he's supposed to be a very valuable special teams contributor.

In his last healthy season (2024), Charles was part of kick coverage duties on the New York Jets , but kick coverage stats prior to 2025 are a different beast when touchback rates were north of 65 percent under the old rules. The ball is now in play on kickoffs an overwhelming majority of the time, so Charles can justify double-digit snaps weekly upon return.

Despite everything I've said about the kick returns, the Seahawks have curiously allowed just one touchdown drive after a kickoff, and that was back on opening night versus the New England Patriots . But the knock-on effect of allowing the opposition to start with reasonably good to great field position is, should a punt be forced, you're most likely backed up. The margin for error for giving up at least a field goal attempt is, at most, 25-ish yards if the other team is anywhere from its own 30 or better. That's asking too much of any defense, not accounting for when they're defending their own territory off of turnovers like we saw in the Washington Commanders game.

This is comparatively not a high priority fix for Seattle compared to the run game inconsistencies, pre-snap penalties, and low red zone struggles, but it's one of those "little things" that is currently not in the Seahawks' favor.

articles.summary: Here's how you can watch the Spartans' exhibition opener against Incarnate Word on Friday night
articles.body:
Michigan State basketball has revealed how fans can watch their first exhibition game of the season, which is slated for later this week.

The Spartans will play their first official game of the season on Friday, with an exhibition opener against Incarnate Word from the Breslin Center in East Lansing, Mich. The game is part of the annual Izzone Campout event, with only season ticket holders and students able to attend the game in person.

So for the rest of us that will not be in attendance, we now know how we can watch the action from our home: on the Big Ten Plus app. The Big Ten streaming service will be broadcasting the game, with tipoff scheduled for 7 p.m. ET on Friday.

This marks the first of three exhibition games for Michigan State this season. They'll also play UConn and Marquette in October, before opening the regular season on November 6 against Quinnipiac.
